SwingXtimes.label: Initial
fields: completed_target_visits

Integer counting completed moves above targets while holding the instructed cube, in the required alternating order starting with the robot's right target. Initialize to 0. Increase by one at the decision step immediately following each completed target move; do not increase for pickup, release, or button pressing. Count each completed move once, not each frame showing a highlight. Episode 44 and episode 72 have values [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4]; episode 53 has [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6]; episodes 56 and 69 have [0, 0, 1, 2, 2]. e.g. 2
completed_target_visits

With empty incoming memory, write 0. Otherwise start with the incoming integer. The next countable destination is the smaller-x target when that integer is even, and the larger-x target when it is odd. Increase once if the observed interval shows completion of a move above that destination: the cube remains grasped, the final hand is hovering at approximately 0.100 height above that target, and that destination is highlighted at the final scene. Use the final destination rather than a stale highlight during transit. Do not count pickup, which ends with the hand raised at approximately 0.150 height, or release, which ends with an open empty hand. Do not count multiple frames of the same arrival, and do not increase beyond the required number of visits (twice the requested repetition count, or two for the instruction to go right then put down left). Otherwise preserve the incoming integer. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal: Read the requested cube color and repetition count from the goal each time. Let N be twice the repetition count; for 'move ... right-side target, then put it down on the left-side target', N is 2. Update completed_target_visits from the observed interval before selecting the next subgoal. Right means the smaller-x target and left means the larger-x target, irrespective of y. Start with A, pointing at the instructed cube on the table. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits is less than N, choose B: point at the right target if the count is even, or the left target if it is odd. This also governs the transition from pickup to the first target move and between successive target moves. Select a point on the target itself, not the elevated cube or wrist. Use the latest clear view of that target anywhere in the current observed interval if it is occluded in the final scene; in particular, episode 72's first right target is visible earlier in the pickup interval. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits equals N, choose C to lower and release it on the table at the final left target. When the count equals N and the final scene shows the cube released and the hand empty, choose D. Thus release precedes button pressing even when the goal only explicitly says to press the button after the repetitions. For an unexpected dropped cube before N, choose A at the instructed cube and retain the count. For an unconfirmed arrival while still holding the cube, repeat B toward the destination selected by count parity without incrementing the count. If a required object is obscured, use its latest clear position in the current interval; if none is available, choose the best-supported location from the visible scene rather than inventing a completed visit or stopping to ask. All points use [y, x].

StopCube.label: Initial
fields: passage_count

The number of completed target-center passages by the cube up to and including this decision's final observation. Count passages in both directions, including during preparation; do not count proximity alone. A passage occurs when cube x minus target x changes sign along the continuous motion. Initialize to 0. The values by decision step are: episode 23: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 32: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 66: 0,0,1,1; episode 94: 0,0,1,2,2; episode 99: 0,0,1,1. e.g. 2
last_side

The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
passage_count

Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
last_side

The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
inst.subgoal: Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. If passage_count equals N-1 and the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the current interval's timestamped cube positions and finds its next crossing of the visible target x; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. In particular, an endpoint turnaround can already be the press-launch time for a fast cube. The final shown decisions in episodes 23 and 32 are such turnarounds; those in episodes 66, 94, and 99 show motion toward the requested next passage. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

VideoUnmask.label: Initial
fields: remaining_targets

An ordered list of [y, x] container locations for the pickups requested by the goal that have not yet been completed. At the first decision step, associate each requested cube color with the container that covered its location in the demonstration, and list those container centers in the order requested. Ignore containers covering unrequested colors and empty distractors. Remove the first entry at the first decision step showing that its container has been successfully grasped and lifted, not at the step choosing the pickup. Putting a container down does not restore its entry. Otherwise preserve the list and its coordinates. Thus episode 7 has [[81, 95], [66, 143]] at step 1 and [[66, 143]] at both steps 2 and 3. The initial lists for episodes 4, 17, 30, and 93 are respectively [[84, 156]], [[95, 156]], [[125, 126]], and [[70, 108]]. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
remaining_targets

With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and use the demonstration to match each cube to the container placed over its location. Write the ordered list of those containers' centers as [y, x] points, excluding distractors. With existing memory, inspect the execution frames for a completed pickup of the first listed container: the hand approaches its location, closes to a nonzero grasp opening, and rises with the grasp maintained. On that observed completed pickup, remove the first entry exactly once. A static container detection at the old location does not negate the observed grasp-and-lift sequence. Do not remove an entry merely because you are now selecting A, because a container is already held without a new pickup, or because the hand releases a container. Preserve all other entries and their coordinates, including across put-down execution. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
inst.subgoal: Apply the memory update from the observations before selecting the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container corresponding to the first point in remaining_targets. Select the current visible container at that remembered location, allowing small centroid shifts, and point inside it; the point need not equal the demonstrated center exactly. When a completed pickup leaves a container held and another target remains, choose B to put down the container. A raised hand with fingers maintaining a nonzero grasp opening after closure and lift is evidence of holding, even if object detections still report the old container center. When put-down execution shows release and the hand is empty, choose A on the first remaining target; do not select the previously picked container again merely because it is still visible. Completion of the last requested pickup satisfies the goal, so no further command is needed unless another decision is requested. For an unexpected extra decision with no targets remaining, choose B as the available release action. For ambiguous or otherwise uncovered situations, choose B if the observations indicate a held container; otherwise choose A on the visible container nearest the first remaining point. If that container is temporarily occluded, use its remembered point. Do not infer hidden cube colors from current container appearance.

ButtonUnmaskSwap.label: Initial
fields: pending_target_positions

An ordered list of [y, x] positions identifying the containers for the cube colors requested in the goal, in goal order, excluding targets already successfully picked up. Before covering, use the visible cube centers. Once covered, follow the identity of the covering container through every shuffle, recording its center at the decision scene; contents travel with the container, not with the original table location. Use the complete motion trajectory, not nearest matching between shuffle endpoints. Remove the first entry at the decision step showing its successful pickup, before any subsequent put-down. Track remaining entries during pickup and put-down despite small apparent center shifts. Thus episode 8's first target ends the shuffles near [111, 128] and its second near [82, 155]; episode 15's targets end near [128, 200] and [102, 182]; episode 66's target ends near [123, 178]; episode 73's near [103, 123]; episode 79's targets near [133, 183] and [106, 154]. An empty list means all requested pickups have occurred. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
buttons_completed

The number of required button presses completed so far, written as 0, 1, or 2. Record 0 at the initial decision, 1 at the decision following the first button press, and 2 at the decision following the second button press and thereafter. Count completed presses, not buttons currently appearing depressed. e.g. 1
pending_target_positions

With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. Process the observed frames chronologically: associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through the observed motion. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. Resolve the rotating pairs using trajectory continuity and direction across all intermediate frames, allowing identities to exchange endpoints; nearest endpoint matching alone is incorrect. Update each remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene. If the interval shows the first pending container being grasped and lifted successfully, remove that entry once; a held-container observation continuing into a put-down interval is not a new pickup. Recognize success from the grasp-and-lift transition, supported by the revealed requested cube. Keep tracking the remaining targets during the hand's movements, ignoring small occlusion-induced center wobble. Write [] when none remain. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
buttons_completed

Initialize to 0 with empty incoming memory. Process the interval for a completed button press: a hand descent to the button followed by withdrawal, with button depression or contact-height evidence, increments the incoming count once, capped at 2. The first menu button is the larger-x button in these scenes; the second is the smaller-x button. A pressed-down label is sufficient supporting evidence but is not mandatory: the low contact and subsequent withdrawal in episode 66 also show the second press. Preserve the count when buttons spring back and throughout container manipulation. Do not increment merely because a button is visible. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: Update memory from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Every episode starts with A. If buttons_completed is 0, choose A, press the first button. If it is 1, choose B, press the second button. Only when it is 2 may container pickup begin. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations, prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target, and retry an uncompleted button or pickup rather than declaring success without evidence. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

fields: pending_target_positions

An ordered list of [y, x] positions identifying the containers for the cube colors requested in the goal, in goal order, excluding targets already successfully picked up. Before covering, use the visible cube centers. Once covered, follow the identity of the covering container through every shuffle, recording its center at the decision scene; contents travel with the container, not with the original table location. Use the complete motion trajectory, not nearest matching between shuffle endpoints. Remove the first entry at the decision step showing its successful pickup, before any subsequent put-down. Track remaining entries during pickup and put-down despite small apparent center shifts. Thus episode 8's first target ends the shuffles near [111, 128] and its second near [82, 155]; episode 15's targets end near [128, 200] and [102, 182]; episode 66's target ends near [123, 178]; episode 73's near [103, 123]; episode 79's targets near [133, 183] and [106, 154]. An empty list means all requested pickups have occurred. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
buttons_completed

The number of required button presses completed so far, written as 0, 1, or 2. Record 0 at the initial decision, 1 at the decision following the first button press, and 2 at the decision following the second button press and thereafter. Count completed presses, not buttons currently appearing depressed. e.g. 1
pending_target_positions

With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. Process the observed frames chronologically: associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through the observed motion. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. Resolve the rotating pairs using trajectory continuity and direction across all intermediate frames, allowing identities to exchange endpoints; nearest endpoint matching alone is incorrect. Update each remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene. If the interval shows the first pending container being grasped and lifted successfully, remove that entry once; a held-container observation continuing into a put-down interval is not a new pickup. Recognize success from the grasp-and-lift transition, supported by the revealed requested cube. Keep tracking the remaining targets during the hand's movements, ignoring small occlusion-induced center wobble. Write [] when none remain. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
buttons_completed

Initialize to 0 with empty incoming memory. Process the interval for a completed button press: a hand descent to the button followed by withdrawal, with button depression or contact-height evidence, increments the incoming count once, capped at 2. The first menu button is the larger-x button in these scenes; the second is the smaller-x button. A pressed-down label is sufficient supporting evidence but is not mandatory: the low contact and subsequent withdrawal in episode 66 also show the second press. Preserve the count when buttons spring back and throughout container manipulation. Do not increment merely because a button is visible. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: Update memory from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Every episode starts with A. If buttons_completed is 0, choose A, press the first button. If it is 1, choose B, press the second button. Only when it is 2 may container pickup begin. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. PickHighlight.label: Initial
fields: remaining_targets

The list of highlighted cubes not yet successfully picked up, represented by their table-center coordinates [y, x]. Before the button-reveal interval has been observed, use null rather than an empty list. At the decision immediately following the button press, populate the list by matching every white highlighted area seen during that interval to its cube; store cube centers, not highlight centers. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. At each decision following a successful pickup, remove the picked cube. Do not remove a cube merely because a pickup was commanded, and do not restore it when placed down. Preserve remaining coordinates through occlusion and minor centroid wobble. Thus episode 6 has null, [[89, 146], [63, 150]], [[63, 150]], [[63, 150]]; episode 28 has null, [[64, 91]]; episode 38 has null, [[81, 125], [113, 120]], [[113, 120]], [[113, 120]]; episode 57 has null, [[84, 92]]; episode 98 has null, [[99, 104], [112, 146]], [[112, 146]], [[112, 146]]. e.g. [[63, 150]]
remaining_targets

Initialize to null when the incoming memory is empty. Inspect all execution frames provided at this decision, not just the final scene. If the incoming value is null and the frames show the button-press interval and white highlighted areas, associate each highlighted area with the cube immediately above or overlapping it and record that cube's table center as [y, x]. Deduplicate repeated sightings. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. Once initialized, retain this list. If the supplied frames show a cube being grasped at a listed table location and subsequently lifted while held, remove that entry at this decision. inst.subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the next subgoal. Each episode starts with A, press button: the initial scene has no held cube and remaining_targets is null. When remaining_targets is a nonempty list and the gripper is empty, choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, targeting the currently visible table cube corresponding to the first stored coordinate. Point at that cube's current center, allowing minor centroid wobble; do not point at the former white area or substitute another cube of the same color. This selects the blue cube near [89, 146] in episode 6, the green cube near [64, 91] in episode 28, the red cube near [81, 125] in episode 38, the blue cube near [84, 92] in episode 57, and the green cube near [99, 104] in episode 98. If pickup failed, retain the target and retry B. If placement failed and the cube remains held, retry C. If the target is temporarily occluded, use its stored table coordinate for B rather than switching targets. If remaining_targets is empty and the gripper is empty, the task is complete; no further pickup or button press is required. If nevertheless forced to select a menu option after completion, choose C as the non-pickup fallback. For other unmodeled situations, choose C if holding a cube, otherwise B at the first remaining target if one exists, otherwise A only when remaining_targets is null.

VideoRepick.label: Initial
fields: target_anchor

A [y, x] point identifying the demonstrated cube at the start of execution. Identify the cube actually grasped in the demonstration, then follow its identity through the release and all subsequent demonstration movements, including exchanges with other cubes. Use its visible center in the initial execution scene, not its original grasp location. Keep this anchor unchanged throughout execution; small subsequent placement shifts do not change which cube it identifies. Initial anchors are [93, 140] in episode 2, [122, 119] in episode 4, [92, 156] in episode 62, [112, 116] in episode 83, and [112, 158] in episode 85. e.g. [122, 119]
completed_cycles

The number of completed execution pick-up-and-put-down cycles as of this decision step, excluding the demonstration. Initialize to 0. Increase by one at the decision step following a completed put-down command, never when merely selecting that command. Internal releases or retries during a pick-up command do not count. Values across steps are [0, 0, 1, 1, 2] for episodes 2, 83, and 85, and [0, 0, 1] for episodes 4 and 62. e.g. 1
target_anchor

With empty memory, inspect the demonstration to identify the cube grasped when the fingers close at table height and the hand lifts. Track that same cube through the rest of the demonstration and locate it in the initial execution scene. Follow continuous motion through exchanges, using direction and trajectory continuity rather than assigning identity by nearest endpoint or retaining the original grasp location. A single exchange moves the target to the other endpoint; two exchanges return it. Store its initial execution visible center as [y, x]. In the supplied demonstrations this gives [93, 140], [122, 119], [92, 156], [112, 116], and [112, 158] for episodes 2, 4, 62, 83, and 85 respectively. At every later step copy the incoming anchor unchanged. e.g. [122, 119]
completed_cycles

With empty memory write 0, ignoring demonstration actions. Otherwise inspect the execution interval shown at this step. Increment the incoming count once if the interval shows the hand starting in its raised grasp posture with partially closed fingers, descending to table height, opening to release, and retreating to a raised fully open posture. This is a completed put-down. Leave the count unchanged for an interval ending in the raised partially closed grasp posture, even if that pick-up interval contains unsuccessful closures, incidental lifts, releases, or retries. Do not increment for the command being chosen now. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: Read the goal each time: the required number N of execution cycles is 2 for 'two times' and 1 for 'again'. Initialize or update memory from the currently shown interval before applying these rules. An episode starts with A: select the cube identified by target_anchor in the initial execution scene. Later, if the interval ends with the raised hand in a grasp posture, choose B, regardless of completed_cycles. In these recordings approximately 46% finger opening after closing at table height and raising is sufficient evidence of that posture; an explicit held-object label is not required, and a cube center still reported on the table does not override it. If the hand is raised and fully open after a release, choose A when completed_cycles < N and C when completed_cycles >= N. Thus a completed A leads to B; a completed B leads to another A only if more cycles remain, otherwise to C. For every A, point at the current visible center of the same cube identified by target_anchor, allowing small shifts after placement; use the release trajectory in the current interval to disambiguate nearby cubes. Do not point at the raised wrist or an airborne cube centroid as a table grasp location. B and C require no point. If observations are ambiguous or do not fit a rule, prioritize B when the final hand appears to retain an object; otherwise choose C only if the required cycle count has been reached, and choose A at the best visible match to target_anchor if it has not. Never count demonstration cycles or internal pick-up retries toward N.

Store the [y, x] center of the target on which the instruction's cube rested immediately before the demonstration button press. Identify it from the last completed placement before that press, not from later placements or the cube's final position. Use the selected target's center in the execution-start scene, matching it through the demonstration despite occlusion and small centroid shifts. Write this at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged thereafter. For episodes 7, 31, 47, 52, and 89 respectively, the values at both decision steps are [126, 145], [115, 152], [80, 162], [101, 163], and [76, 104]. e.g. [126, 145]
pre_press_target

When memory is empty and the demonstration is shown, locate the button press by the closed gripper descending onto the button and its depression. Find the instruction's cube's last completed target placement before that event; if the cube is hidden during the press, use its preceding release and resting position. Match that target to the execution-start scene and write its visible center as [y, x]. Ignore subsequent cube placements when selecting the target. Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
inst.subgoal: Start in A: with the execution-start gripper empty, pick up the cube of the color named in the goal, pointing at its current visible center. Use only the execution scene for this pickup, not its earlier demonstration location. If the observed execution interval shows descent to that cube, closure to a grasp-sized opening (approximately 46%), and a lift with that opening maintained, choose B, dropping onto the target selected by pre_press_target. Explicit held-object evidence also permits B. The recorded cube coordinates may remain at the tabletop position after pickup and a held label may be absent; these do not override the closure-and-lift evidence. Match the remembered point to the corresponding visible target and point within that target, or use the remembered point if it is occluded. If pickup clearly closed on nothing or left the hand empty, choose A again at the requested cube. C is not required: the demonstration press identifies the desired target, and must not be reenacted. A completed release of the requested cube onto the selected target finishes the task; do not press the button afterward. For an otherwise unmatched nonterminal situation, choose B if there is credible evidence the requested cube is held, otherwise A at that cube. If pre_press_target is unknown and dropping is necessary, use the visible target nearest the requested cube as a deterministic fallback rather than asking for clarification.

Record the demonstrated cube-moving method at the first decision step and retain it unchanged throughout the episode. Values are "lift", "hook", or "push". Use "lift" when the demonstration grasps and raises the cube before transporting and placing it; "hook" when it grasps and raises the peg and then uses that tool to move the cube; "push" when the closed gripper moves the cube along the surface without lifting it. Classify by the motion over time, not isolated held-object labels. Episode 30 has "lift" at both steps; episodes 38 and 56 have "hook" at both steps; episodes 83 and 96 have "push" at their sole steps. e.g. "hook"
demonstrated_method

When memory is empty at the first decision step, classify only the demonstration frames, separately from the reset execution scene. Write "lift" if the hand grasps the cube and raises it before carrying it to the target; write "hook" if the hand grasps and raises the peg before using it to move the cube; write "push" if the closed hand moves the cube at tabletop height without lifting it. Use the complete motion: a momentary 'held' label does not establish lifting, and incidental peg movement does not establish tool use. At every subsequent decision step copy the incoming value unchanged. If demonstration evidence is inconclusive, write "unknown" and retain it. e.g. "hook"
inst.subgoal: Use demonstrated_method as initialized from the demonstration at the first decision step, or retained from incoming memory later. Determine current possession from the execution frames only; never treat the demonstration's final hand state as the execution state. A descent to an object, closure to a nonzero opening, and subsequent raised wrist with the opening maintained establish a successful pickup even if the object detector continues reporting the old object location. In these episodes cube grasping leaves about 46% opening, whereas peg grasping leaves about 22–23%; identify the object primarily from the pickup approach rather than these numbers alone. For demonstrated_method="lift", start with D (pick up the cube) when the execution hand is empty. Point at the current cube if a point is required. Once execution shows the cube pickup completed and the hand raised while maintaining its grasp, choose E (place the cube onto the target), pointing at the current target if required. For demonstrated_method="hook", start with A (pick up the peg) when the hand is empty; the peg is the object labeled stick for hooking. Point at that object's current location if required. Once execution shows the peg pickup completed and the wrist raised with its grasp maintained, choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). B acts on the current cube toward the current target; if a destination point is required, select the target. For demonstrated_method="push", start with C (close gripper and push the cube to the target), using the current cube and target; if a destination point is required, select the target. Do not insert a pickup for pushing. Use execution-scene coordinates, never demonstration coordinates, and express points as [y, x]. After B, C, or E has visibly delivered the cube to the target, the task is complete and no further manipulation is needed. If queried again before success, apply the same possession-based rules: repeat the method's pickup when empty, or its transport operation when holding the appropriate object. For unclear possession, inspect the entire available execution interval for closure and lift rather than demanding an explicit held label. For any remaining unmatched situation, make a best-effort choice consistent with the retained method: E if holding the cube, B if holding the peg, otherwise its prescribed starting action; with method="unknown", use the same possession rules and default to D when empty.

InsertPeg.label: Initial
fields: insertion_side

Record the demonstrated insertion side, as "right" or "left", at the first decision step and retain it at every subsequent step. Determine the side from the peg's final approach into the box, not from its original pickup location: approach from smaller x than the box is robot-right; approach from larger x is robot-left. Episodes 1, 15, and 60 have "right" at both steps; episodes 33 and 54 have "left" at both steps. This is the only retained fact: the demonstrated peg and grasp end are available when pickup is selected, and the successful grasp is visible at the next decision. e.g. "right"
insertion_side

When the current observation includes the demonstration and incoming memory is empty, inspect the final low-height insertion approach relative to the box. Write "right" if the held peg approaches the box from smaller x, or "left" if it approaches from larger x. Use this final approach rather than the pickup position or initial lift direction. If the demonstration does not establish a side, write "unknown". At steps without a demonstration, copy the incoming value unchanged; do not infer a new side from the currently held peg's location. e.g. "right"
inst.subgoal: Start in A when the execution scene shows an empty, open gripper. At this first decision, use the visible demonstration to identify the peg that moves with the gripper after closure, trace it back to its pre-grasp position, and determine whether its head or tail was grasped. Match that peg to the reset execution scene and point to that same endpoint, using its current visible position rather than a shifted or occluded centroid during demonstration contact. Episode 1 selects the tail of the peg with head near [124, 204], targeting approximately [116, 211]; episode 15 selects the head near [127, 75], targeting [128, 76]; episode 33 selects the head near [132, 190], targeting [133, 190]; episode 54 selects the head near [72, 158], targeting [73, 159]; episode 60 selects the head near [87, 146], targeting [88, 147]. These points identify endpoints, not universal fixed coordinates. When the current execution observation shows a peg held after pickup, switch from A to B if insertion_side is "right", or to C if insertion_side is "left". Explicit held-object observations or closure followed by the peg moving with the raised hand establish a successful grasp; the wrist being outside the frame does not imply an empty hand. B and C require no point. Do not choose insertion side from the current pickup location. The demonstrated insertion command completes the supplied episodes; no subsequent menu transition is required. For an unanticipated decision, prioritize visible state: if still holding a peg, use the remembered insertion side; if that value is "unknown", use the side of the box on which the held peg currently lies, choosing B for smaller x and C for larger x. If empty-handed and a demonstration remains visible, reapply the demonstrated pickup rule. If empty-handed with no demonstration available, choose A at the clearest accessible peg endpoint as a best-effort fallback rather than claiming to recall an unrecorded target.

PatternLock.label: Initial
fields: remaining_moves

An ordered list of menu letters for the demonstrated target-to-target moves not yet completed in execution, including the move to command at this decision step. Extract one move per demonstrated transition between neighboring targets; preserve consecutive identical moves and ignore pauses, image jitter, and the reset from demonstration to execution. At the first decision step store the complete list. At each subsequent decision step remove the one move completed since the preceding decision. Do not remove the move being selected at the current step. Episode 3 values at steps 1–4 are ["E","D","G","H"], ["D","G","H"], ["G","H"], ["H"]. Episode 10 values are ["A","H","H"], ["H","H"], ["H"]. Episode 34 values are ["A","H","D","F"], ["H","D","F"], ["D","F"], ["F"]. Episode 97 values are ["B","H","A"], ["H","A"], ["A"]. First compute the current completed_placements value from incoming memory and the observed execution interval. Start each supplied episode with A, pointing at the goal-colored cube in the current scene. Episode 44 and episode 72 have values [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4]; episode 53 has [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6]; episodes 56 and 69 have [0, 0, 1, 2, 2]. e.g. 2
completed_target_visits

With empty incoming memory, write 0. Otherwise start with the incoming integer. The next countable destination is the smaller-x target when that integer is even, and the larger-x target when it is odd. Increase once if the observed interval shows completion of a move above that destination: the cube remains grasped, the final hand is hovering at approximately 0.100 height above that target, and that destination is highlighted at the final scene. Use the final destination rather than a stale highlight during transit. Do not count pickup, which ends with the hand raised at approximately 0.150 height, or release, which ends with an open empty hand. Do not count multiple frames of the same arrival, and do not increase beyond the required number of visits (twice the requested repetition count, or two for the instruction to go right then put down left). Otherwise preserve the incoming integer. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal: Read the requested cube color and repetition count from the goal each time. Let N be twice the repetition count; for 'move ... right-side target, then put it down on the left-side target', N is 2. Update completed_target_visits from the observed interval before selecting the next subgoal. Right means the smaller-x target and left means the larger-x target, irrespective of y. Start with A, pointing at the instructed cube on the table. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits is less than N, choose B: point at the right target if the count is even, or the left target if it is odd. This also governs the transition from pickup to the first target move and between successive target moves. Select a point on the target itself, not the elevated cube or wrist. Use the latest clear view of that target anywhere in the current observed interval if it is occluded in the final scene; in particular, episode 72's first right target is visible earlier in the pickup interval. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits equals N, choose C to lower and release it on the table at the final left target. When the count equals N and the final scene shows the cube released and the hand empty, choose D. Thus release precedes button pressing even when the goal only explicitly says to press the button after the repetitions. For an unexpected dropped cube before N, choose A at the instructed cube and retain the count. For an unconfirmed arrival while still holding the cube, repeat B toward the destination selected by count parity without incrementing the count. If a required object is obscured, use its latest clear position in the current interval; if none is available, choose the best-supported location from the visible scene rather than inventing a completed visit or stopping to ask. All points use [y, x].

Integer counting completed moves above targets while holding the instructed cube, in the required alternating order starting with the robot's right target. Initialize to 0. Increase by one at the decision step immediately following each completed target move; do not increase for pickup, release, or button pressing. Count each completed move once, not each frame showing a highlight. Episode 44 and episode 72 have values [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4]; episode 53 has [0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6]; episodes 56 and 69 have [0, 0, 1, 2, 2]. e.g. 2
completed_target_visits

With empty incoming memory, write 0. Otherwise start with the incoming integer. The next countable destination is the smaller-x target when that integer is even, and the larger-x target when it is odd. If the incoming count is below the required number of visits, increase once when the observed interval ends with the cube still grasped, the hand at approximately 0.100 height on the expected destination's side, and that destination highlighted in the final scene. The elevated wrist or cube need not coincide with the target in image coordinates: projection offsets above and slightly beside the target are expected and do not invalidate this arrival evidence. Use the final destination highlight, not a stale highlight during transit. Do not count pickup, which ends with the hand raised at approximately 0.150 height, or release, which ends with an open empty hand. Do not count multiple frames of the same arrival, and do not increase beyond the required number of visits (twice the requested repetition count, or two for the instruction to go right then put down left). Otherwise preserve the incoming integer. Treat the incoming integer as the pre-interval count and apply the arrival test above exactly once. Use the resulting count both to select the next subgoal and as the outgoing completed_target_visits value. Do not write the incoming count after using an incremented count for subgoal selection. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal: Read the requested cube color and repetition count from the goal each time. Let N be twice the repetition count; for 'move ... right-side target, then put it down on the left-side target', N is 2. Update completed_target_visits from the observed interval before selecting the next subgoal. Right means the smaller-x target and left means the larger-x target, irrespective of y. Start with A, pointing at the instructed cube on the table. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits is less than N, choose B: point at the right target if the count is even, or the left target if it is odd. This also governs the transition from pickup to the first target move and between successive target moves. Select a point on the target itself, not the elevated cube or wrist. Use the latest clear view of that target anywhere in the current observed interval if it is occluded in the final scene; in particular, episode 72's first right target is visible earlier in the pickup interval. When the cube is held and completed_target_visits equals N, choose C to lower and release it on the table at the final left target. When the count equals N and the final scene shows the cube released and the hand empty, choose D. Thus release precedes button pressing even when the goal only explicitly says to press the button after the repetitions. For an unexpected dropped cube before N, choose A at the instructed cube and retain the count. For an unconfirmed arrival while still holding the cube, repeat B toward the destination selected by count parity without incrementing the count. If a required object is obscured, use its latest clear position in the current interval; if none is available, choose the best-supported location from the visible scene rather than inventing a completed visit or stopping to ask. All points use [y, x].

StopCube.label: Initial
fields: passage_count

The number of completed target-center passages by the cube up to and including this decision's final observation. Count passages in both directions, including during preparation; do not count proximity alone. A passage occurs when cube x minus target x changes sign along the continuous motion. Initialize to 0. The values by decision step are: episode 23: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 32: 0,1,2,3,4; episode 66: 0,0,1,1; episode 94: 0,0,1,2,2; episode 99: 0,0,1,1. e.g. 2
last_side

The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
passage_count

Start at 0 for empty memory, otherwise use the incoming passage_count. Process all newly shown observations chronologically, starting with incoming last_side as the preceding side. Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
last_side

The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
inst.subgoal: Start in A: move to the top of the visible button to prepare. Select A whenever the hand is not yet in the prepared position. The prepared pose in these observations has the wrist above the button, height approximately 0.15, and closed fingers; do not mistake the wrist's image position for the fingertips' contact point. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. If passage_count equals N-1 and the next target passage is approximately 35 or fewer time units away, select C. Estimate the upcoming arrival from the chronological cube motion shown at this step, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. A useful estimate fits smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the current interval's timestamped cube positions and finds its next crossing of the visible target x; do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant. In particular, an endpoint turnaround can already be the press-launch time for a fast cube. The final shown decisions in episodes 23 and 32 are such turnarounds; those in episodes 66, 94, and 99 show motion toward the requested next passage. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. If motion timing is uncertain, default to B while refining the estimate from the next observations, rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

Compute the sign of cube x minus target x. Each nonzero sign opposite to the preceding nonzero side increments the count once; then update the working side. Ignore exact equality until a nonzero side appears. Include observations during A and B, and count multiple crossings within one decision interval separately. Write the resulting count, without adding any predicted future passage from the command being selected. e.g. 2
last_side

The cube's most recently observed nonzero side of the target center, represented as -1 when cube x is smaller than target x and 1 when it is larger. If exactly equal, retain the preceding nonzero side; use 0 if none has yet been observed. Record the side at the decision's final observation, not the side expected after its selected command. e.g. -1
motion_history

With empty memory, start with an empty ordered list; otherwise preserve incoming motion_history. Append all newly shown execution observations chronologically, including the final observation, keeping only one sample for any repeated timestamp. Exclude demonstration observations. Write only observed timestamps and cube x measurements, never predicted positions or command outcomes. Use the combined incoming history and newly shown execution observations to estimate motion for subgoal selection. Do not recount retained history when updating passage_count: that update still uses only newly shown observations and incoming last_side. Each history entry contains a timestamp and a scalar cube x measurement, not a spatial coordinate pair. Serialize the field as list text with single-quoted keys, key order 'time' then 'cube_x', and one space after each colon and comma. Do not include extra outer quotation marks within the value. Use [] for an empty list. This representation does not change the observations retained. e.g. [{'time': 0, 'cube_x': 47}, {'time': 16, 'cube_x': 80}, {'time': 32, 'cube_x': 147}]
inst.subgoal: Select A, move to the top of the visible button to prepare, only when the observed hand is not already prepared. Recognize a closed gripper with wrist height approximately 0.15 (including 0.154–0.155), wrist roughly 34–36 image units above the button, and a small horizontal offset as already prepared. This configuration takes precedence over apparent wrist/button image-center misalignment: the wrist is not the fingertips' contact point. Do not select A merely because those image centers differ. Once prepared, choose between B and C using the updated passage_count and the requested ordinal N from the goal. C must be initiated before the requested passage because button pressing takes approximately 25–35 recording time units. For a prepared hand, select C only when both conditions hold: the updated passage_count equals N-1, and a reliable crossing-time calculation gives 0 < estimated remaining arrival time <= 35 recording time units. An estimate above 35 is outside the launch window; do not round it into the window. The count alone never authorizes C. Select B if passage_count is less than N-1, or if it equals N-1 but the estimated next passage is outside this window or its timing is uncertain. Estimate the upcoming arrival using incoming motion_history together with all newly shown execution observations, accounting for slowing and reversal at endpoints. Calculate the next crossing timestamp before choosing C. First check the combined timestamped evidence for repeated motion: matching positions and directions across cycles can establish a period. When recurrence is established, interpolate earlier crossings of the currently visible target x between their bracketing samples and advance those crossing times by whole periods. Use the earliest predicted crossing strictly after the current timestamp, considering both crossing directions. Prefer this observed recurrence over a conflicting rough velocity estimate. If recurrence is not yet established, fit smooth periodic motion x(t)=a+b*cos(w*t)+c*sin(w*t) to the combined timestamped evidence, allowing for pixel noise, and solve for its earliest crossing of the currently visible target x strictly after the current timestamp. If neither method reliably establishes whether arrival is within the launch window, select B. Earlier travel and reversal evidence must continue to inform the estimate when the newest interval is short or nearly stationary. Do not extrapolate a near-zero endpoint velocity as constant or interpret two identical endpoint positions as evidence that the cube has permanently stopped. From the combined timestamped evidence, estimate the next target-crossing timestamp and subtract the current timestamp to obtain the remaining arrival time. Apply this calculation after an observed reversal as well as during approach to or departure from an endpoint; retain earlier travel and reversal evidence in the estimate. If the hand is prepared, updated passage_count=N-1, and the evidence reliably establishes 0 < estimated remaining arrival time <= 35 recording time units, select C. This conjunction requires C, rather than merely permitting it. Choose B if the crossing is farther away or the combined evidence genuinely cannot establish whether it is within the window; endpoint proximity alone still never authorizes C. Update crossing counts only from newly shown observations, never by recounting retained history. When the cube is moving away from the target after the preceding crossing, calculate the next crossing by including both the remaining travel to the endpoint and the return travel to the target; distance to the target divided by current speed is not a valid arrival estimate in this situation. Slowing down or nearing an endpoint does not by itself authorize C. A fast endpoint turnaround can nevertheless be the press-launch time if the estimated next crossing is within the lead window and passage_count equals N-1; do not require that the cube already be moving toward the target. Select B while fewer than N-1 passages have completed, or while the requested next passage remains farther away than this lead window. Reevaluate after every B; remaining static can span several passages, so update memory from every shown frame. None of these menu options requires a supplied point; A and C concern the visible button. Use the timing-uncertainty fallback to B only when the combined motion evidence genuinely cannot establish whether arrival is within the lead window. Pixel noise or modest uncertainty in the exact crossing timestamp does not justify waiting when the well-supported arrival estimates lie wholly within that window and the preparedness and ordinal conditions hold; select C in that case. Otherwise refine the estimate from the next observations rather than pressing on the wrong ordinal. If already stopped at the requested target, remain static. For other uncovered situations, prepare with A if necessary, otherwise remain static with B.

VideoUnmask.label: Initial
fields: remaining_targets

An ordered list of [y, x] container locations for the pickups requested by the goal that have not yet been completed. At the first decision step, associate each requested cube color with the container that covered its location in the demonstration, and list those container centers in the order requested. Ignore containers covering unrequested colors and empty distractors. Remove the first entry at the first decision step showing that its container has been successfully grasped and lifted, not at the step choosing the pickup. Putting a container down does not restore its entry. Otherwise preserve the list and its coordinates. Thus episode 7 has [[81, 95], [66, 143]] at step 1 and [[66, 143]] at both steps 2 and 3. The initial lists for episodes 4, 17, 30, and 93 are respectively [[84, 156]], [[95, 156]], [[125, 126]], and [[70, 108]]. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
remaining_targets

With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and use the demonstration to match each cube to the container placed over its location. Write the ordered list of those containers' centers as [y, x] points, excluding distractors. With existing memory, inspect the execution frames for a completed pickup of the first listed container: the hand approaches its location, closes to a nonzero grasp opening, and rises with the grasp maintained. On that observed completed pickup, remove the first entry exactly once. A static container detection at the old location does not negate the observed grasp-and-lift sequence. Do not remove an entry merely because you are now selecting A, because a container is already held without a new pickup, or because the hand releases a container. Preserve all other entries and their coordinates, including across put-down execution. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
inst.subgoal: Apply the memory update from the observations before selecting the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container corresponding to the first point in remaining_targets. Select the current visible container at that remembered location, allowing small centroid shifts, and point inside it; the point need not equal the demonstrated center exactly. When a completed pickup leaves a container held and another target remains, choose B to put down the container. A raised hand with fingers maintaining a nonzero grasp opening after closure and lift is evidence of holding, even if object detections still report the old container center. When put-down execution shows release and the hand is empty, choose A on the first remaining target; do not select the previously picked container again merely because it is still visible. Completion of the last requested pickup satisfies the goal, so no further command is needed unless another decision is requested. For an unexpected extra decision with no targets remaining, choose B as the available release action. For ambiguous or otherwise uncovered situations, choose B if the observations indicate a held container; otherwise choose A on the visible container nearest the first remaining point. If that container is temporarily occluded, use its remembered point. Do not infer hidden cube colors from current container appearance.

Anchor both identities at their pre-motion positions and use the first small, distinguishable displacement to establish their angular direction around that center. Among assignments consistent with the established rotation direction, select the smallest common forward angular advance consistent with the preceding motion, rather than an assignment requiring an additional half-turn between adjacent samples. Propagate each assigned identity from that frame into the next; do not restart association from its pre-motion position when the pair settles. PickHighlight.label: Initial
fields: remaining_targets

The list of highlighted cubes not yet successfully picked up, represented by their table-center coordinates [y, x]. Before the button-reveal interval has been observed, use null rather than an empty list. At the decision immediately following the button press, populate the list by matching every white highlighted area seen during that interval to its cube; store cube centers, not highlight centers. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. At each decision following a successful pickup, remove the picked cube. Do not remove a cube merely because a pickup was commanded, and do not restore it when placed down. Preserve remaining coordinates through occlusion and minor centroid wobble. Thus episode 6 has null, [[89, 146], [63, 150]], [[63, 150]], [[63, 150]]; episode 28 has null, [[64, 91]]; episode 38 has null, [[81, 125], [113, 120]], [[113, 120]], [[113, 120]]; episode 57 has null, [[84, 92]]; episode 98 has null, [[99, 104], [112, 146]], [[112, 146]], [[112, 146]]. e.g. [[63, 150]]
remaining_targets

Initialize to null when the incoming memory is empty. Inspect all execution frames provided at this decision, not just the final scene. If the incoming value is null and the frames show the button-press interval and white highlighted areas, associate each highlighted area with the cube immediately above or overlapping it and record that cube's table center as [y, x]. Deduplicate repeated sightings. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. Once initialized, retain this list. If the supplied frames show a cube being grasped at a listed table location and subsequently lifted while held, remove that entry at this decision. Use its pre-lift table position to identify it, not its raised position. An unsuccessful closure or temporary disappearance is not sufficient for removal. Placement does not add an entry back. Keep stored coordinates unchanged despite occlusion or small visible centroid changes. An empty list means all revealed targets have been picked up; null means the reveal has not yet been recorded. e.g. [[63, 150]]
inst.subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the next subgoal. Each episode starts with A, press button: the initial scene has no held cube and remaining_targets is null. If remaining_targets is still null and no completed reveal is available, choose A. When remaining_targets is a nonempty list and the gripper is empty, choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, targeting the currently visible table cube corresponding to the first stored coordinate. Point at that cube's current center, allowing minor centroid wobble; do not point at the former white area or substitute another cube of the same color. This selects the blue cube near [89, 146] in episode 6, the green cube near [64, 91] in episode 28, the red cube near [81, 125] in episode 38, the blue cube near [84, 92] in episode 57, and the green cube near [99, 104] in episode 98. If the current scene shows a cube held after pickup, choose C, place the cube onto the table, even though that cube has already been removed from remaining_targets. After placement, an empty gripper and a nonempty remaining_targets list lead back to B for its first entry; never pick up an already removed cube again. If pickup failed, retain the target and retry B. If placement failed and the cube remains held, retry C. If the target is temporarily occluded, use its stored table coordinate for B rather than switching targets. If remaining_targets is empty and the gripper is empty, the task is complete; no further pickup or button press is required. If nevertheless forced to select a menu option after completion, choose C as the non-pickup fallback. For other unmodeled situations, choose C if holding a cube, otherwise B at the first remaining target if one exists, otherwise A only when remaining_targets is null.

If the currently shown execution interval includes descent onto that cube, closure to a cube-sized opening (about 46%), and withdrawal with that opening maintained, treat the pickup as completed and choose B, even if the object description omits 'held' or reports a center near its old tabletop position. An explicit held annotation also supports B. For B, point at the target matching selected_target, using its current visible center when available and the stored point if occluded. Do not select another target based on proximity to the held cube. If a pickup visibly closes on nothing or otherwise clearly fails and the desired cube remains available, choose A again at that cube. After a successful release onto the selected target, the goal is complete; no button press is required. C is not used for these goals: button presses in the demonstration neither reset the placement count nor require imitation. If an unexpected decision follows a completed correct placement and a menu command is mandatory, choose A on the goal cube and subsequently B onto the same selected target, rather than pressing the button. For other uncovered situations, use A when the hand is empty and the goal cube can be located, and B when holding the goal cube and selected_target is known. If selected_target is unknown and a drop is mandatory, use the nearest visible target as a deterministic fallback, without claiming it is the demonstrated target.

fields: selected_target

Store one [y, x] point identifying the target on which the goal-named cube was placed at the goal-requested ordinal during the demonstration. Count completed placements onto targets chronologically, not frames, initial cube positions, flyovers, button presses, or the final release onto the unmarked central workspace. Identify a placement by lowering the carried cube onto a target and releasing it. Identify the physical target at the requested completed release, then follow its identity through the remainder of the demonstration into the first execution scene, including occlusion, large movements, and exchanges of positions with other targets. Use continuous trajectories and the motion of all targets to resolve identity, not proximity to the original release location or the final layout alone. Target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Store that physical target's center in the first execution scene as the canonical [y, x] point. If the requested placement or the selected target's identity cannot be established from the demonstration and first execution scene, write "unknown". Write this point at decision step #1 and retain it unchanged at every subsequent decision step.  e.g. [116, 163]
selected_target

When the incoming memory is empty and the current step includes the demonstration, read the cube color and placement ordinal from the goal. Initialize in two stages. First build a temporary chronological list of the goal-colored cube's completed releases onto targets: a carried cube is lowered onto a target, released, and left there as the hand withdraws. Record each release once with the physical target receiving it. Do not count initial positions, flyovers, button presses, or releases onto unmarked workspace; button presses do not reset the count. Select the requested ordinal entry using one-based counting, checking the releases through that entry to ensure that it is the requested placement rather than the preceding one. Second, follow the physical target identified at that entry through every remaining demonstration observation into the first execution scene. Keep the release list temporary, not in persistent memory. Maintain temporary identities for all targets while scanning the remaining demonstration; treat target lists as unordered detections, not persistent identity indices. Track continuous motion through temporary occlusion, small shifts, large movements, and exchanges of positions. For each interval of coordinated movement, associate all targets jointly across the entire interval using successive displacement directions and smooth path continuation. First identify targets supported as stationary throughout the interval, allowing small visible-center wobble, and reserve their detections for those identities. Determine stationarity from intermediate observations throughout the interval, not merely matching start and end positions. Then associate the remaining moving branches jointly, allowing curved paths; do not jump from a moving branch onto a nearby stationary target merely because that assignment is shorter. Use intermediate observations to resolve correspondences rather than independently assigning each identity to the nearest detection at each frame. Do not restore identities from the final layout or match the original release coordinate directly to the nearest execution target: a return to the same set of positions does not establish that each physical target returned to its own position. Distinguish coherent movement across observations from small apparent center shifts caused by occlusion. Before writing, verify separately that the release-list entry has the requested ordinal and that its physical target's tracked endpoint matches the chosen target in the first execution scene. If no coherent target movement occurs after the selected release, preserve that target's identity through occlusion-related center shifts rather than substituting an earlier placement's target. Resolve the selected target's endpoint against the first execution scene, then discard the temporary release list and tracks after writing its canonical center. Target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Write the selected physical target's center in the first execution scene as [y, x]; do not store intermediate trajectories. On subsequent steps copy the incoming selected_target unchanged, regardless of the current grasp or target-center wobble. If the demonstration and first execution scene do not establish the requested placement or the selected physical target's identity, write "unknown" rather than inventing a placement or a target correspondence. e.g. [116, 163]

MoveCube.label: Initial
fields: demonstrated_method

Record the demonstrated cube-moving method at the first decision step and retain it unchanged throughout the episode. Values are "lift", "hook", or "push". Use "lift" when the demonstration grasps and raises the cube before transporting and placing it; "hook" when it grasps and raises the peg and then uses that tool to move the cube; "push" when the closed gripper moves the cube along the surface without lifting it. Classify by the motion over time, not isolated held-object labels. Episode 30 has "lift" at both steps; episodes 38 and 56 have "hook" at both steps; episodes 83 and 96 have "push" at their sole steps. e.g. "hook"
demonstrated_method

When memory is empty at the first decision step, classify only the demonstration frames, separately from the reset execution scene. Write "lift" if the hand grasps the cube and raises it before carrying it to the target; write "hook" if the hand grasps and raises the peg before using it to move the cube; write "push" if the closed hand moves the cube at tabletop height without lifting it. Use the complete motion: a momentary 'held' label does not establish lifting, and incidental peg movement does not establish tool use. At every subsequent decision step copy the incoming value unchanged. If demonstration evidence is inconclusive, write "unknown" and retain it. e.g. "hook"
inst.subgoal: Use demonstrated_method as initialized from the demonstration at the first decision step, or retained from incoming memory later. Determine current possession from the execution frames only; never treat the demonstration's final hand state as the execution state. A descent to an object, closure to a nonzero opening, and subsequent raised wrist with the opening maintained establish a successful pickup even if the object detector continues reporting the old object location. In these episodes cube grasping leaves about 46% opening, whereas peg grasping leaves about 22–23%; identify the object primarily from the pickup approach rather than these numbers alone. For demonstrated_method="lift", start with D (pick up the cube) when the execution hand is empty. Point at the current cube if a point is required. Once execution shows the cube pickup completed and the hand raised while maintaining its grasp, choose E (place the cube onto the target), pointing at the current target if required. For demonstrated_method="hook", start with A (pick up the peg) when the hand is empty; the peg is the object labeled stick for hooking. Point at that object's current location if required. Once execution shows the peg pickup completed and the wrist raised with its grasp maintained, choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). B acts on the current cube toward the current target; if a destination point is required, select the target. For demonstrated_method="push", start with C (close gripper and push the cube to the target), using the current cube and target; if a destination point is required, select the target. Do not insert a pickup for pushing. Use execution-scene coordinates, never demonstration coordinates, and express points as [y, x]. After B, C, or E has visibly delivered the cube to the target, the task is complete and no further manipulation is needed. If queried again before success, apply the same possession-based rules: repeat the method's pickup when empty, or its transport operation when holding the appropriate object. For unclear possession, inspect the entire available execution interval for closure and lift rather than demanding an explicit held label. For any remaining unmatched situation, make a best-effort choice consistent with the retained method: E if holding the cube, B if holding the peg, otherwise its prescribed starting action; with method="unknown", use the same possession rules and default to D when empty.

Episode 34 values are ["A","H","D","F"], ["H","D","F"], ["D","F"], ["F"]. Episode 97 values are ["B","H","A"], ["H","A"], ["A"]. remaining_moves

When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, read the entire demonstration chronologically and write its complete ordered list of target-to-target menu letters. Identify the starting highlighted target and each successive reached target using highlight changes together with sustained wrist motion. Highlights can retain the previous target, so do not interpret the displayed order of highlighted coordinates as travel order. Each neighboring-target transition is one move, even when consecutive transitions have the same direction. Ignore pauses and small coordinate fluctuations; exclude the reset into execution. Infer grid row and column changes rather than treating small perspective-induced x shifts during vertical motion as diagonals. Larger y means forward, smaller y backward, larger x left, and smaller x right. Encode forward A, backward B, left C, right D, forward-left E, forward-right F, backward-left G, backward-right H. At every later decision step with carried memory, the oracle has completed the preceding command: remove exactly the first entry of the incoming list and write the resulting suffix. This removal occurs once per decision, not once per observed frame or highlight change. Keep the new first entry in the written list because its command has not yet executed. If the incoming list is empty, retain []. If neither demonstration nor carried memory is available, write []. e.g. ["E","D","G","H"]

fields: placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. Empty list at step #1. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. Count released cubes even if a cube of that color later appears somewhere on the table, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. e.g. ["green", "green"]
placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Start with an empty list when the memory is empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]
inst.subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, take the one with the larger remaining count (ties: either). Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. Prefer a cube of that color that was already visible at the same place in the earlier execution steps of this decision step (or, at step #1, simply any cube of that color), and avoid detections that flicker in and out or that lie on top of the bin's position; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the cube of a needed color nearest the gripper, and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.
