visits_done

Carry in the previous value (start at 0 on the first step, where memory is empty). Add 1 if and only if, at the scene of this decision step, the cube is 'held in the gripper' AND a 'highlighted target' is shown under/near the gripper AND that highlighted target either was absent or was a different target in the first execution frame shown for this step. Otherwise keep the carried-in value unchanged (the pick-up step, the put-down step where the cube ends on the table with fingers fully open, and the press-button step do not change it). e.g. 3
inst.subgoal: Coordinates are [y, x]. The right-side target is the one with the SMALLER x; the left-side target is the one with the LARGER x. First read the goal to get the required number of target visits REQ: if it says 'repeating this back and forth motion N times' then REQ = 2*N (two=4, three=6); if it instead says 'then put it down on the left-side target' then REQ = 2. Every episode starts with subgoal A. Rules (apply whichever matches the current step and memory): 1. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and visits_done is 0 (cube resting on the table, fingers open, nothing done yet): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the cube's center coordinates. 2. If the cube IS held in the gripper and visits_done < REQ: choose B, move to the top of the target. If visits_done is even (0, 2, 4...), point at the right-side target (smaller x); if visits_done is odd (1, 3, 5...), point at the left-side target (larger x). Equivalently, point at the target that is NOT currently highlighted. Use that target's listed coordinates. 3. If the cube IS held in the gripper and visits_done >= REQ (the cube is now above the left-side target after the last required visit): choose C, put the cube on the table. 4. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and visits_done >= REQ (cube resting on the table after the put-down, fingers fully open, gripper raised): choose D, press the button. If no rule matches: when the cube is held, choose B pointing at the target that is not highlighted; when the cube is on the table and visits_done is 0, choose A at the cube; when the cube is on the table and visits_done > 0, choose D.

inst.subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away, so the press, which takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Do not read the cube's direction or speed from the frames to make the decision: cube speed varies threefold across episodes and changes around the turnaround, and the predicted arrival time computed from first_cross_t decides on its own. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if and only if crossings == N-1 AND remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, so it is started once the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away). Whether the cube is still running out, stopped at its turnaround, or already heading back toward the target makes no difference: being past the turnaround or moving back is not enough while remaining > 30. After that, Rule 2 applies again with the next cube in the goal. If all cubes named in the goal have already been picked (picks_done equals the number of cubes named), choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last named cube. Unforeseen situation: if a container is held, choose C; if containers are visible and nothing is held, choose B at the container nearest the recorded position of the next goal cube; if no containers are visible, choose A.

Increases by one only at a decision step whose own final scene (the observation at the decision step itself, after the last execution step) shows a container held in the gripper, i.e. the step reached right after a 'pick up the container' subgoal finished. At a decision step whose final scene shows nothing held, the value is carried unchanged, even if earlier execution steps at that decision step still showed the container held before it was released (the step reached right after a put-down). e.g. 1
blue_cube_pos

If this step shows a loose blue cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the blue cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged; never overwrite it from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. [128, 141]
green_cube_pos
If this step shows a loose green cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the green cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged. e.g. [88, 106]
red_cube_pos
If this step shows a loose red cube and no containers (the scene before the button is pressed), write the red cube's [y, x] as shown. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged. e.g. [130, 79]
picks_done

Number of container pick-ups completed. Start at 0. Look only at the scene at this decision step itself (the last observed step, after all execution steps). If that scene shows a container held in the gripper, write carried-in value + 1. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged, even if earlier execution steps at this decision step showed a container held before it was released. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: An episode starts in A (press the button): the first step shows the three loose cubes and no containers. Rule 1: if the step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere and nothing held, choose A (press the button); at the same time record each cube's position in the memory fields. Rule 2: if the step shows containers on the table and the gripper is NOT holding a container, choose B (pick up the container). The target is the cube named in the goal at position picks_done+1 in the goal's order (first named cube when picks_done is 0, second named cube when picks_done is 1). Look up that cube's recorded position (blue_cube_pos / green_cube_pos / red_cube_pos) and point at the center of the container nearest to that recorded position, writing the point as [y, x]. Ignore containers that cover no recorded cube. Rule 3: if the step shows a container held in the gripper, choose C (put down the container). After that, Rule 2 applies again with the next cube in the goal. If all cubes named in the goal have already been picked (picks_done equals the number of cubes named), choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last named cube. Unforeseen situation: if a container is held, choose C; if containers are visible and nothing is held, choose B at the container nearest the recorded position of the next goal cube; if no containers are visible, choose A.

ButtonUnmaskSwap.label: Initial
fields: buttons_pressed

Count of button presses completed so far, including any press whose 'is pressed down' frame appears among the execution steps shown at this decision step. 0 at step #1, 1 at the step after the first press, 2 from the step after the second press to the end. e.g. 1
green_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At step #1 (before any container exists) it is the green cube's own position. From the step where containers appear, it is the position of the container that came down on the green cube, then followed frame by frame through every shuffle: during each button press two containers glide around each other and end up having swapped places, so the green container's position becomes the other mover's resting position. Updated at every step to the last frame shown. Once this container has been lifted and the cube is exposed, keep the cube's exposed position. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors

Ordered list of cube colors whose hiding container has been lifted so far. Empty until the step whose execution frames show a container 'held in the gripper' with a cube revealed beneath; then that cube's color is appended, and the list is kept afterwards. e.g. ["green"]
buttons_pressed
Carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step says a button 'is pressed down'; otherwise the carried-in count. Start at 0. e.g. 1
green_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. When containers appear, take the one standing on the carried-in green position. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. If the green cube is exposed by lifting its container, write the exposed cube's position. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors

Carried-in list; append the color of the cube that appears beneath a container shown 'held in the gripper' among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. Start empty. e.g. ["green"]
inst.subgoal: Start every episode in A (press the first button). Apply the first matching rule, after updating memory for this step: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

fields: demo_placements

Ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) was released during the DEMONSTRATION, in the order the releases happened. A release is a frame where the fingers go from ~46% open to ~100% open while that cube was 'held in the gripper' just before; the entry is the position of the target closest to the cube's resting spot right after that release, taken from a demo frame where all four targets are visible (e.g. the last demo frame). Do NOT include the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127], no target there), do not include the cube's starting spot, do not include button presses, and do not include a release that is onto the same target the cube was just lifted from if no target lies under the cube. Written at step #1 (the only step that shows the demonstration) and copied unchanged at every later step. Empty list only if no demonstration was shown. e.g. [[116, 163], [75, 163]]
goal_target

The single target position, in [y, x], that the goal instruction's ordinal picks out of demo_placements: 'first' = entry 1, 'second' = entry 2, 'third' = entry 3, 'fourth' = entry 4. Written at step #1 from the demonstration and copied unchanged afterwards. unknown before the demonstration has been seen. e.g. [116, 163]
demo_placements

At the first decision step (the one that shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS and the memory is empty), scan the demo frames for the cube whose colour the goal instruction names, and write the ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], where it was released: a release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper'; record the target whose position (read from a demo frame listing all four targets, such as the last demo frame) is closest to where the cube now rests. Skip the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127] with no target there), skip the cube's starting spot, and skip button presses (fingers 0% open, no cube held). At every later step, copy the carried-in value unchanged. Empty list if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. [[116, 163], [75, 163]]
goal_target

At every later step copy the carried-in value unchanged. unknown if demo_placements is empty. e.g. [116, 163]
inst.subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied to whatever the step shows: 1. If the cube named in the goal instruction is NOT held (fingers ~100% open, gripper raised or empty, cube resting on the table): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the current position of the goal-named cube as shown in the scene at this decision step (typically near [82, 127] at the start of execution). This is always the case at the first decision step. 2. The way the demonstration moved the cube, fixed at the first decision step from the demonstration steps and never changed afterwards. Write `pick` when the demonstration shows the cube marked as held in the gripper while the gripper rises well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed around it (about 40-60% open), and the cube is then released over the target. Write `hook` when the demonstration shows the stick (peg) marked as held in the gripper, with fingers closed to about 20-25%, and the stick dragged against the cube toward the target. Write `push` when the demonstration shows the fingers closing to about 0% (closing on nothing) at table height (below about 0.04) and the cube then sliding to the target while the gripper never rises with it; neither cube nor stick is ever held while raised. Same value at every step of the episode. e.g. hook
holding

What the robot has in its fingers at this decision step, judged from the execution steps shown. `none` at the first decision step and whenever the fingers are fully open or closed on nothing. `cube` once the execution steps show the gripper descend onto the cube, the fingers close to about 40-60% and the gripper rise again with the fingers still partly closed. `peg` once the execution steps show the gripper descend onto the stick, the fingers close to about 20-25% and the gripper rise again with the fingers still closed. Back to `none` once a later step shows the fingers reopen to 100%. e.g. peg
method

The way the demonstration moved the cube. At the first decision step, read it from the demonstration steps: `pick` if the cube is marked as held in the gripper while the gripper is well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed (about 40-60% open) and the cube is then released over the target; `hook` if the stick (peg) is marked as held in the gripper with fingers closed to about 20-25% and is dragged against the cube toward the target; `push` if the fingers close to about 0% at table height (height below about 0.04) and the cube slides to the target without ever being lifted or any stick being held. At every later step copy the value carried in unchanged; never write `unknown` after the first step. e.g. hook
holding

What the robot has in its fingers at this decision step. Write `none` at the first decision step (nothing has been executed yet). Write `cube` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the cube, close the fingers to about 40-60%, and rise again with the fingers still partly closed. Write `peg` if the execution steps shown descend the gripper onto the stick, close the fingers to about 20-25%, and rise again with the fingers still closed. Write `none` if the fingers at this step are 100% open or closed to about 0%. If the execution steps show no grasp, copy the value carried in. e.g. peg
inst.subgoal: The menu options need no target point; if a point is demanded anyway, point at the object the option names (the cube for C, D, E; the stick for A; the target for B and E would be the cube's destination, but prefer the cube). An episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory; first fill `method` from the demonstration steps, then choose by it. Rules, applied in whatever situation the policy stands in: - If `method` is `push`: choose C (close gripper and push the cube to the target). This is the only subgoal for a push episode. - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `none`: choose D (pick up the cube). - If `method` is `pick` and `holding` is `cube` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 40-60% on the cube and the gripper rise): choose E (place the cube onto the target). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `none`: choose A (pick up the peg). - If `method` is `hook` and `holding` is `peg` (the execution steps just showed the fingers close to about 20-25% on the stick and the gripper rise): choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). If a situation has no rule: if `method` cannot be told, decide by what the scene shows - fingers partly closed with the cube raised means E, fingers closed to about 20-25% with the stick raised means B; otherwise if the demonstration showed the stick held choose A, if it showed the cube lifted choose D, and if neither choose C. Never choose E without the cube in hand and never choose B without the peg in hand.

The [y, x] of the peg end the demonstration gripper closed on. grasp_end

insert_side

fields: plan

The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces, written at the first decision step from the demonstration steps and copied unchanged at every later step. Derive it from the highlighted targets: the first highlighted target at demo t=0 is the start; each time a new target becomes highlighted during the demo, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (using the coordinates at the first frame each appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. e.g. ["E", "D", "G", "H"]
moves_done

How many of the planned moves the robot has finished executing by the scene at this step. 0 at the first decision step (nothing executed yet); at every later decision step it is the previous value plus one, since each decision step follows exactly one completed move. e.g. 2
plan

The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces. If this step shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS (the first step, memory empty), build it now and never change it afterwards: the highlighted target at demo t=0 is the start; each time a different target becomes highlighted in the demo frames, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (coordinates at the frame it first appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. If the step shows no demonstration, copy the carried-in plan exactly. e.g. ["E", "D", "G", "H"]
moves_done

How many planned moves have been finished by the scene at this step. Write 0 when the step shows demonstration steps and the carried memory is empty (first step). Otherwise the step shows execution steps of one completed move, so write the carried-in moves_done plus one. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal: Every episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory and the demonstration shown; the subgoal there is the first letter of the plan just built from the demonstration (plan index 0). At every decision step, the subgoal is the letter of plan at index moves_done (0-based, where moves_done is the value written at THIS step: 0 at the first step, carried value plus one at later steps). So the first step performs plan[0], the second step plan[1], and so on. No subgoal needs a point. After a move finishes, the next decision step always advances to the next plan letter regardless of where the gripper ended; never repeat or skip. If moves_done is at or beyond the length of the plan (nothing remains), repeat the last plan letter. If the plan could not be built (no demonstration visible and empty plan), derive the direction from the two highlighted targets currently visible if there are two (direction from the older-looking one near the gripper to the other, same dy/dx rule), otherwise choose A: move forward. In any other unforeseen situation, pick plan[moves_done] if it exists, else A.

BinFill.label: Initial
fields: placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. Empty list at step #1. At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. Count released cubes even if a cube of that color later appears somewhere on the table, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. e.g. ["green", "green"]
placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Start with an empty list when the memory is empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]
inst.subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, take the one with the larger remaining count (ties: either). Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. Prefer a cube of that color that was already visible at the same place in the earlier execution steps of this decision step (or, at step #1, simply any cube of that color), and avoid detections that flicker in and out or that lie on top of the bin's position; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the cube of a needed color nearest the gripper, and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

BinFill.label: Round 1
fields: placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, one entry per completed 'put it into the bin' subgoal, oldest first. The value is always written as a JSON array of double-quoted color strings; at step #1 it is the literal [] (an explicit empty array, never a blank). At the decision step that directly follows an execution of B (the execution steps show a cube held in the gripper and then released over the bin, and the scene at the decision step shows the gripper open with nothing held), append the color of the cube that was held during that execution. Never append after a pick-up execution (one that ends with a cube held) and never after pressing the button. That held-then-released event is always one completed bin placement: count it regardless of where the gripper was reported when the fingers opened (often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and regardless of any same-color cube detection appearing on the table at or near the release point in the same frames, since the bin is opaque and detections near it are unreliable. Example sequence over an episode: [] -> [] -> ["green"] -> ["green"] -> ["green", "green"]. e.g. ["green", "green"]
placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is empty, write the literal [] as this step's value. The value is always a JSON array of double-quoted strings, exactly like the carried-in value and the example: ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green'] and never a blank. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. The oracle always runs the put-into-bin subgoal to completion, so this held-then-released pattern is always a successful placement: append whatever the gripper position at release (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and whatever cubes appear, move or vanish on the table in the same frames. e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"]. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]
inst.subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: if the last entry of `placed` is a color whose required count is not yet met, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started); otherwise, including when `placed` is empty, pick any color that still has fewer entries than required. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the needed color reported as a table cube (not held) at the same coordinates, within about 2 px, in every execution frame of this decision step including the first one (at step #1, with no execution frames, any cube of that color in the scene is a candidate). A detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, that is reported within about 25 px of the bin's center, or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. Among several stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin's reported center without overlapping it. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the stable cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not overlapping it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not overlapping the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

With several, the scene gives no arrival order, so the annotator, reading the whole episode, lists first the pre-existing cubes the oracle actually picks during the episode in the order it picks them (first-picked first), and after them the never-picked cubes of a needed color ordered by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first (two within about 3 px of the same distance: larger x first), skipping detections within about 28 px of that center. At each later step, in order: (1) removal, only at a pick-up step (one whose execution frames show the fingers going from open to about 46% while the gripper is over a table cube, followed by a held line): remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in that closing frame. At a put-into-bin step, where the first execution frame already shows a cube held, remove nothing (the held cube's entry was already removed at its pick-up step). Never remove an entry that still has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; the 12 px test is never stretched to the nearest entry. (2) retention: matching is one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new. An entry with a match is kept and refreshed to that position; the bin-echo and release-echo exclusions do not apply here, so an entry matching a detection near the just-released cube's last reported position or near the gripper at release is kept. An entry with no such detection is dropped. (3) appending: every goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended, except bin echoes and release echoes. A bin echo is a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was present in the scene at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step; a detection of a color not yet in `placed` that first appears during the step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the scene at the decision step is a genuine new cube however near the bin it lies, and is appended in order of first appearance. The release frame is the first execution frame in which the fingers are about 100% open and no object line says held (a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it). A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appears in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moves a few px along with the retreating gripper over the following frames; it is never appended however far it is from the bin center. A detection is not an echo if it matches an existing entry within about 12 px or was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. A goal-color detection that appears during the step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and then stays put is a genuine new arrival and is appended. In a pick-up step (one that ends with a cube held and has no release frame) there is no release echo and no moved-with-the-gripper exclusion: every new goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that is not a bin echo is appended, even one within a dozen px of the gripper or of the just-grasped cube. (4) when several detections are appended in one step, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared (earliest first), tracking each across frames within about 12 px; two that first appear in the same frame follow that frame's listing order. Example over a step in which a green cube appeared at [86, 143] in an early frame and another at [86, 95] in a later frame, with [86, 119] picked up: [[86, 143], [86, 95]]. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
placed

Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. Write the word none as this step's value only at the very first decision step, where the carried-in memory is blank and there are no execution steps at all. The value is plain color words separated by single spaces and nothing else: no brackets, no quotes, no commas. A carried-in none that comes with execution steps is appended to by the check below like any other value: the first appended color replaces none, so the step after the first placement writes a single word such as blue. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except after a two-part check applied in order: first, does any execution frame of this step contain an object line ending 'is held in the gripper'; second, does the scene at this decision step (the last listed frame) show the fingers about 100% open with no held line. If both hold, the oracle completed the put-into-bin subgoal: append one space and that held cube's color exactly once (if the carried-in value is none, replace it by the color). The gripper's position when the fingers opened is irrelevant (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center); fingers opening only to 67-99% in an intermediate frame are irrelevant; same-color detections that appear, shift a few px, or vanish on the table in those frames are irrelevant (detections near the opaque bin are echoes of the held cube or bin contents, not table cubes). None of these is a reason to skip the append. e.g. carried-in red becomes red red; carried-in blue blue after a held-then-released blue cube becomes blue blue blue. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Emit the value as bare words only; any brackets, quotes or commas make it a wrong value. e.g. blue blue blue green
arrivals

Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the subgoal rule picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames): if exactly one goal-color cube is in the scene, the list is that cube. If several are, the scene does not show which came first; list first every cube of the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (two colors needing the same count: the one the goal names first), then the next color by count; the order the goal names the colors is not the criterion. Within a color order by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping any detection within about 28 px of that center; when two cubes of one color are within about 3 px of the same distance, put the one with the larger x (the robot's left) first. Example with a goal of three blue and one green, green at [65, 109] and blue at [84, 112]: [[65, 109], [84, 112]]. A cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed. At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) PICK-UP REMOVAL, only if some execution frame of this step shows the fingers about 100% open over a table cube and a later frame of this step shows them at about 46% with a cube then reported held: remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in the frame where the fingers first reached 46%. If the very first execution frame already shows a cube held (fingers 46%, a held line), this is a put-into-bin step and nothing is removed, whatever entry lies near the gripper. Never remove an entry that still matches a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame; never stretch the 12 px test to the nearest entry. (2) RETAIN AND REFRESH: match one-to-one with a hard cutoff: each remaining entry is matched to at most one detection of its color, the nearest within about 12 px, and a detection 13 px or more from every still-unmatched entry is new (handled in (3)). A matched entry is kept and set to that position; this match ignores the bin-echo and release-echo tests, which concern only new detections. Drop an entry with no such detection. (3) APPEND NEW: a goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended unless it is a bin echo or a release echo. A detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center is a bin echo only if it was present in the scene at the first decision step, or its color already appears in the carried `placed`, or this step released a cube of that color; a detection of a color not in `placed` that first appears in some execution frame of this step and is still at the same place (within about 12 px) in the last frame is a genuine new cube however near the bin it is: append it, in the order of the frame where it first appeared. The release frame is the first execution frame of this step where the fingers are about 100% open with no held line; a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it. A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported in that frame, or that has moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame; it is excluded even when far from the bin center. A detection that was already at its place in the first execution frame of the step, or that matches a carried entry, is never an echo. A detection that appears mid-step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and stays put is a genuine new cube: append it. In a step that ends with a cube held (a pick-up step: first execution frame shows no held line, last frame shows one) there is no release frame, so the release-echo and moved-with-the-gripper tests do not apply; a new goal-color detection that appears near the gripper or near the just-grasped cube during such a step and is in the last frame is appended like any other, excluding only bin echoes. (4) When several new detections are appended, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared, earliest first, tracking each across frames within about 12 px; same-frame arrivals follow that frame's listing order. Order is otherwise never changed. Example: carried [[77, 139]], a pick-up step closing on [77, 139], with a red cube that appeared at [100, 66] several frames earlier far from bin and gripper, and two red detections within 28 px of the bin: write [[100, 66]]. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
inst.subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory fields `placed` and `arrivals` as updated at this step. `placed` is space-separated color words (the word none when nothing has been placed); a color's count is the number of times its word appears, and none counts as zero for every color. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. `placed` here is the value as updated at this step: a step whose execution frames show a cube held and whose last frame shows the fingers about 100% open with nothing held counts that cube as placed, so choose C when every goal count is then met, even if cubes of the goal colors remain on the table, including one that reappeared near the bin after the release. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last word of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table). At the first decision step, where several goal-color cubes may be present with no arrival order to read, the working color is the color with the SMALLEST required count in the goal instruction (equal counts: the one the goal names first); `arrivals` as written at this step begins with that color, nearest the bin first, so that is where the first pick goes. At every later step the goal's counts and naming order play no part in the choice of color. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the working color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step. New cubes genuinely appear on the table during the episode, so a detection that was absent from earlier frames is still a candidate, and one that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. Excluded, at every step including step #1: a bin echo, meaning a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center that was there at step #1, or whose color already appears in `placed`, or whose color was released in this step (a cube 30 px or more from the center that stays in place is real, and a cube of a not-yet-placed color that appeared mid-step and stayed put is a candidate wherever it lies); a release echo, meaning a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame (the first execution frame of this step with the fingers about 100% open and no held line) within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame, excluded however far it is from the bin; a detection already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step, or matching a carried `arrivals` entry within about 12 px, is not an echo; and a detection whose position tracks the gripper from frame to frame. Among several candidates, choose the one that comes first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px): the oracle picks the cube of the working color that has been on the table longest. Only when the candidates cannot be told apart by `arrivals` (none of them matches an entry) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color: with one goal-color cube in the scene, that cube; with several, the cube of the color with the smallest required count in the goal (equal counts: the color named first) that is nearest the bin's reported center while at least about 28 px from it; when two such cubes are within about 3 px of the same distance to the bin, the one with the larger x (the robot's left). If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else the cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not within 28 px of it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not within 28 px of the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

PickXtimes.label: Initial
fields: placements_done

Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target so far in the episode, counting the placement shown in this step's execution steps. It is 0 at step #1 and at every step whose execution steps do not contain a release of the cube over the target. It increases by exactly one at each decision step whose execution steps show the cube held in the gripper, then the fingers opening to ~100% while the gripper is low (height below about 0.03) at the target position, leaving the cube resting on the target (the step whose correct subgoal follows a 'place' command). It never decreases. e.g. 1
placements_done

Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target. Start at 0 on the first step. At each decision step, take the value carried in; add 1 if the execution steps shown at this step contain the cube marked 'is held in the gripper' and then, later in the same step, the fingers opened to about 100% with the gripper low (height below about 0.03) and the cube now lying at roughly the target's position, no longer held. Otherwise keep the carried value unchanged. Never decrease it. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: First read the goal instruction to get the required number of placements N: if it says 'repeating this action two times' N=2, 'three times' N=3, and so on; if it mentions no repetition, N=1. The cube to use is the one whose color the goal names (ignore other cubes). Update placements_done first, then decide. An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied in whatever situation you are in: 1. If the goal-colored cube is shown 'is held in the gripper' at the scene of this decision step (fingers about 46% open, gripper raised), choose B: place the cube onto the target. 2. If the cube is NOT held at the scene of this decision step (fingers ~100% open) and placements_done (after this step's update) is less than N, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the current [y, x] of the goal-colored cube as shown in the final scene of this step (after a placement it will be sitting on or near the target; point at the cube, not the target). 3. If the cube is NOT held and placements_done (after this step's update) is equal to or greater than N, choose C: press the button to stop. 4. If the gripper closed but the cube is not reported as held (a missed grasp), treat it as not held: apply rule 2 or 3 by placements_done. If you meet a situation none of these rules cover, default to: if the cube is held choose B; otherwise if placements_done < N choose A pointing at the goal-colored cube's current position; otherwise choose C.

A step in which the gripper closed on nothing (cube never labelled held) does not count even if the cube already sits on the target from an earlier placement. A step ending with the cube held does not count. It never decreases. e.g. 2

Do not require any particular finger percentage or gripper height at an intermediate frame; a release frame may show fingers only 80-90% open with the cube still marked held, and that still counts once the final scene meets (b). Do not add 1 if the cube was never marked held during this step (a missed grasp, even if the cube already rests on the target from before), or if the final scene shows the cube held. Otherwise keep the carried value unchanged. Never decrease it. e.g. 2

fields: placements_done

Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target so far in the episode, counting the placement shown in this step's execution steps. It is 0 at step #1 and at every step whose execution steps do not contain a release of the cube over the target. It increases by exactly one at each decision step whose execution steps show the goal-colored cube labelled 'is held in the gripper' at some frame AND whose final scene shows that cube no longer labelled held, lying within a few pixels of the target position, with the fingers ~100% open (the step whose correct subgoal follows a 'place' command). No finger percentage or gripper height is required at any intermediate frame; the 'is held' label may lag a frame behind the actual release and is ignored at intermediate frames. A step in which the gripper closed on nothing (cube never labelled held) does not count even if the cube already sits on the target from an earlier placement. A step ending with the cube held does not count. It never decreases. e.g. 2
placements_done

Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target. Start at 0 on the first step. At each decision step, take the value carried in; add 1 if BOTH hold: (a) at least one execution frame shown at this step has the goal-colored cube marked 'is held in the gripper', and (b) in the final scene of this step the goal-colored cube is NOT marked held, the fingers are about 100% open, and the cube lies within a few pixels of the target position. Do not require any particular finger percentage or gripper height at an intermediate frame; a release frame may show fingers only 80-90% open with the cube still marked held, and that still counts once the final scene meets (b). Rules, applied in whatever situation you are in: 1. If the goal-colored cube is shown 'is held in the gripper' at the scene of this decision step (fingers about 46% open, gripper raised), choose B: place the cube onto the target. 2. If the cube is NOT held at the scene of this decision step (fingers ~100% open) and placements_done (after this step's update) is less than N, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the current [y, x] of the goal-colored cube as shown in the final scene of this step (after a placement it will be sitting on or near the target; point at the cube, not the target). 3. fields: crossings

Number of times, since t=0 and up to and including the scene at this decision step, that the cube's x-coordinate has moved from one side of the target's x-coordinate to the other (a crossing happens between two consecutive observed frames when the sign of cube_x minus target_x flips; being near the target without flipping is not a crossing). Each crossing is one arrival of the cube at the target. At step #1 the value is 0. It increases only at the step whose observed frames contain the flip. e.g. 2
cube_side

Which side of the target line the cube is on in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. At step #1 it is read from the t=0 frame. e.g. larger_x
crossings

Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2
cube_side

The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. Overwrite it every step. e.g. larger_x

For every consecutive pair in that list write the x change |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| and the timestep gap; if the gap is at least 8, write the quotient rounded to one decimal with halves rounding up (3.875 -> 3.9); if the gap is below 8 timesteps (common just before the decision scene, where detection wobble dominates), skip that pair. Write the largest of the carried-in value and all the counted quotients. It never decreases. At the first step (empty memory, one frame) write 0. e.g. 2.0
last_cube_x

Write the cube's x-coordinate in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step), as a plain number. x is the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position: a cube at [85, 52] gives 52. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. It is read at the next step as the earlier member of the pair with the first frame shown there, both for peak_speed and, when that step shows a single frame, for judging the cube's motion. e.g. 52
last_t

Write the timestep index t of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step write 0. It is read at the next step to compute the timestep gap between the carried-in last_cube_x and the first frame shown there: that gap decides whether the pair counts for peak_speed (gap at least 8) and gives the rate for the motion judgement at a single-frame step. e.g. 503
inst.subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, cube_side, peak_speed, last_cube_x, last_t), then decide using the updated crossings and peak_speed values and the cube motion: - Determine the cube's motion from a pair of positions, in this order. Form the pair first: when two or more frames are shown at this step, the pair is the last two frames shown; when exactly one frame is shown, the earlier member of the pair is the carried-in memory (position last_cube_x, side cube_side, time last_t) and the later member is the shown frame, so the x change is cube_x minus last_cube_x and the timestep gap is t of this frame minus last_t. cube_x is always the SECOND number of the cube's [y, x] position, and target_x the SECOND number of the target's [y, x] position; the first numbers are y and are never compared. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in the two members of the pair (for a single-frame step: the carried-in cube_side differs from the side in this frame), it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW, whatever the distances are. (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each member of the pair, take the change (later minus earlier) and divide by the timestep gap between them: this is the outward rate in px per timestep (negative if the distance shrank). Always divide by the timestep spacing; never judge by the raw pixel change between frames. Then compute distance = |cube_x - target_x| at the scene at this step, and lead = distance / peak_speed, the number of timesteps the cube would need at its peak speed to reach the target (if peak_speed is 0, treat lead as very large). The press is issued a fixed lead before arrival, about 20 to 27 timesteps, whether the cube is finishing its outward sweep or already returning, so classify: if the outward rate is zero or negative (returning or stopped) AND lead <= 27, the cube is IN THE PRESS WINDOW. If the outward rate is positive but at most about 60% of peak_speed (clearly slowed, finishing its outward sweep) AND lead <= 24, the cube is IN THE PRESS WINDOW. Otherwise the cube is NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW: returning but lead > 27 (it turned around far out and is still too many timesteps away; it will be pressed at a later decision step), moving outward at more than about 60% of peak_speed (still sweeping out near full speed), or moving outward with lead > 24 (too far out for its speed). - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is classified IN THE PRESS WINDOW above. No point is needed. A step that shows a single frame is common right after the step at which the cube was seen nearing its extreme; when crossings == N-1 and the pair formed from memory places the cube IN THE PRESS WINDOW, that single-frame step is the press moment, not a reason to wait. Showing only one frame is never by itself a reason to choose B. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is NOT IN THE PRESS WINDOW (including the case where the (N-1)th crossing lies between the last two frames, so the cube is just passing the target and about to sweep outward; and the case where the cube has already turned around but is still more than 27 peak-speed timesteps from the target, which is pressed at a later step). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is heading toward the target, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

target_containers

Ordered list of container positions, one per cube named in the goal, in the order the goal names them. picks_done

Count of target containers picked up so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. At any later step, take the carried-in value and add one if the execution steps since the previous decision step show the fingers going from fully open to partly closed (about 40-60% open) with the gripper then raised, i.e. a container was grasped and lifted; otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the container. Count the cubes named in the goal; that is the number of targets N, equal to the length of target_containers. Rule for A (pick up): choose A whenever the gripper is not holding a container (fingers fully open, or gripper raised out of frame) and picks_done is less than N. Point at the container listed at index picks_done in target_containers (the first entry when picks_done is 0, the second when picks_done is 1). Write the point as that container's position with y reduced by about 3 pixels (e.g. container [84, 156] gives point [81, 158]). If the container visible at this step has drifted slightly from the stored position, point at the visible container nearest the stored position. Rule for B (put down): choose B whenever the gripper is holding a container (fingers partly closed, around 40-60% open, gripper raised after a grasp) and picks_done is less than N, meaning another target still has to be picked up. After the put-down the next decision step will show fingers fully open; then apply rule A for the next target. When picks_done equals N and the robot is holding a container, the task is complete and no further decision is expected; if asked anyway, choose B. If a situation matches no rule (e.g. fingers closed on nothing, 0% open, or the memory is inconsistent with the scene), choose A and point at the entry of target_containers at index picks_done, or at the first entry if that index does not exist, and do not change picks_done.

Filled at the first decision step from the demonstration (cube positions in the early frames, container that came down on each cube at the frame containers first appear, then that container followed frame to frame through every shuffle). put_down_count

Number of containers the robot has picked up and then put down so far in this episode. 0 at the first decision step; increases by one at the decision step whose execution steps show the fingers reopening (from about 46% back to about 100%) while over a container, i.e. the step right after a 'put down the container' subgoal finished. e.g. 1
target_containers

Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note the position of each named cube; (2) at the first frame where containers are listed instead of cubes, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube's position; (3) follow that container through the remaining demonstration frames: at each frame it is the listed container nearest to its position in the previous frame, and when two moving containers are nearly equally near, keep the one that continues the same arc (the container that moved toward larger y keeps the larger y, the one that moved toward smaller y keeps the smaller y); containers that never move keep their position; (4) its position in the last demonstration frame is the entry. e.g. [[81, 90], [87, 134]]
put_down_count

Number of containers picked up and then put down so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. Add one to the carried-in value when the execution steps of the current step show the fingers reopening from about 46% to about 100% after being lowered over a container (a put-down just completed); otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: An episode starts in A (pick up the container), with the point on the first entry of target_containers computed from the demonstration at that same step. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.

Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them; each entry is the position, at the last demonstration frame, of the container that ends up hiding that cube. Filled once at the first decision step from the demonstration, by slots and swaps: (1) in the first cube frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first container frame, the named cube's container is the one resting nearest that cube; every container's resting position in that frame is its slot; (3) scan the remaining frames; each block of consecutive frames in which two containers are away from their slots (off by well over 10 pixels) is one shuffle between the two containers whose slots are empty; when the next frame shows all containers back at slots, those two containers have exchanged slots (a second shuffle of the same pair puts them back where they were; shuffles of other pairs do not touch the named container); (4) the entry is the named cube's container's slot after all swaps, written with the coordinates listed for that slot in the last demonstration frame (slots wobble by a few pixels). Never changes afterwards; copied unchanged at every later step. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]
put_down_count

Number of containers the robot has picked up and then put down so far in this episode. 0 at the first decision step; increases by one at the decision step whose execution steps show the fingers reopening (from about 46% back to about 100%) while over a container, i.e. the step right after a 'put down the container' subgoal finished. e.g. 1
target_containers

Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) go through the remaining frames; whenever a frame lists two containers at positions that are not slots (off by well over 10 pixels), a shuffle is under way between the two containers whose slots are now empty; it lasts until a frame again shows all containers at slots; at that frame those two containers have SWAPPED slots, so if the named container was one of the two, its slot is now the other container's old slot; a second shuffle of the same pair swaps them back; shuffles of other pairs do not change its slot; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example: cube at [70, 119]; containers first rest at [66, 120], [84, 109], [93, 163], [119, 145]; the cube's container is [66, 120]; later frames show [66, 120] and [84, 109] both off their slots for three frames, then all back; those two swapped, so the cube's container is now the one at [84, 110] in the last frame; entry [84, 110]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]

Rule 2: if the step shows containers on the table and the gripper is NOT holding a container, choose B (pick up the container). The target is the cube named in the goal at position picks_done+1 in the goal's order (first named cube when picks_done is 0, second named cube when picks_done is 1). If all cubes named in the goal have already been picked (picks_done equals the number of cubes named), choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last named cube. Rule 2: if the last frame shows containers on the table and the gripper is NOT holding a container, the button has already been pressed, so choose B (pick up the container). Rule 3: if the last frame shows a container held in the gripper, choose C (put down the container). After that, Rule 2 applies again with the next cube in the goal. ButtonUnmaskSwap.label: Initial
fields: buttons_pressed

Count of button presses completed so far, including any press whose 'is pressed down' frame appears among the execution steps shown at this decision step. 0 at step #1, 1 at the step after the first press, 2 from the step after the second press to the end. e.g. 1
green_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At step #1 (before any container exists) it is the green cube's own position. From the step where containers appear, it is the position of the container that came down on the green cube, then followed frame by frame through every shuffle: during each button press two containers glide around each other and end up having swapped places, so the green container's position becomes the other mover's resting position. Updated at every step to the last frame shown. Once this container has been lifted and the cube is exposed, keep the cube's exposed position. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors

Ordered list of cube colors whose hiding container has been lifted so far. Empty until the step whose execution frames show a container 'held in the gripper' with a cube revealed beneath; then that cube's color is appended, and the list is kept afterwards. e.g. ["green"]
buttons_pressed
Carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step says a button 'is pressed down'; otherwise the carried-in count. Start at 0. e.g. 1
green_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. When containers appear, take the one standing on the carried-in green position. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. If the green cube is exposed by lifting its container, write the exposed cube's position. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position when visible, then the container that covered it, followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors

Carried-in list; append the color of the cube that appears beneath a container shown 'held in the gripper' among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. Start empty. e.g. ["green"]
inst.subgoal: Start every episode in A (press the first button). Apply the first matching rule, after updating memory for this step: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

ButtonUnmaskSwap.label: Round 1
fields: buttons_pressed

Count of button presses completed so far. A press is completed in the step whose execution frames show either a button 'is pressed down' or the gripper at a button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed. 0 at the first step (no execution frames), 1 at the step after the first such frame, 2 from the step after the second to the end. e.g. 1
green_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At step #1 (before any container exists) it is the green cube's own position. From the step where containers appear, it is the position of the container that came down on the green cube, then followed by chaining through every frame shown: starting from the previous step's last frame, each container is matched to the container of the previous frame with the smallest displacement (the gliding may already be under way in the first frame of a step). During a press two containers glide around each other; a single circling pass ends with them swapped, a double pass ends with them back at their starting spots, and the chain decides which. Value is the tracked container's position in the last frame shown. Once the cube beneath it is visible (container lifted or held in the gripper), the field becomes the cube's position and from then on keeps the cube's last visible position, even after a container is lowered back over it. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, followed by chained smallest-displacement matching frame by frame from the previous step's last frame (one circling pass swaps the pair, two passes return them; trust the chain), written at the last frame shown; once the red cube is visible, the cube's last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

Current [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, followed by chained smallest-displacement matching frame by frame from the previous step's last frame (one circling pass swaps the pair, two passes return them; trust the chain), written at the last frame shown; once the blue cube is visible, the cube's last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors

Ordered list of cube colors whose hiding container has been lifted so far. Written as a JSON list with double-quoted strings, explicitly [] when empty, including at the first step. [] until the step whose execution frames show a cube visible beneath a lifted or 'held in the gripper' container; then that cube's color is appended, and the list is kept afterwards. e.g. ["green"]
buttons_pressed

Write 0 at the first step (empty carried-in memory, no execution frames). Otherwise write the carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown says a button 'is pressed down' OR shows the gripper at a button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed; otherwise the carried-in count. e.g. 1
green_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At the first step, with empty memory, WRITE the green cube's [y, x] from the scene. When containers first appear, take the container standing on the carried-in position. At every later step, match the carried-in position to the nearest container in the FIRST frame shown, then follow it frame to frame, each time choosing the container with the smallest displacement from the previous frame; never match the carried-in position straight to the last frame. Containers gliding around each other usually finish swapped, but trust the chain, not the assumption (one circling pass swaps them, two passes return them). Write the followed container's position in the last frame. If any frame shows the green cube itself (container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), write the cube's position in the last frame it is visible, and keep that cube position at later steps even once a container is lowered back over it. e.g. [109, 126]
red_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: write the red cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap); once the red cube is visible, its last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [82, 152]
blue_container

[y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: write the blue cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap); once the blue cube is visible, its last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [102, 79]
picked_colors
