Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up: the cube that is listed as 'held in the gripper' (or vanishes from the table list while the gripper is closed) during the DEMONSTRATION STEPS, located where it sits on the table in the scene at the start of execution (it is set back down at nearly the spot it was lifted from, and the shuffle at the end of the demonstration returns it there). At every later step the value is refreshed to the current table position of that same cube (the listed cube nearest the previous value, within about 10 px) whenever it is resting on the table; while the cube is held in the gripper the value is left unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]
picks_done

Count of completed pick-ups in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (the last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed on the cube (about 46% open, cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list). It does not change at decision steps whose last frame shows the fingers 100% open. e.g. 1
target_cube

Position [y, x] of the cube to pick. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the cube that appears as 'held in the gripper' (or disappears from the table list while the gripper fingers are about 46% open), note where it was on the table just before the gripper came down on it, and write the position of the cube that sits closest to that spot in the scene at the start of execution (the cube is set down and the shuffle returns it to nearly the same place). At every later step, if the scene at this decision step lists a cube on the table within about 10 px of the carried value, write that cube's current position; if the cube is currently held in the gripper, copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]
picks_done

Count of completed pick-ups. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, look at the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if the gripper is raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and a cube is held in the gripper or missing from the table list, write the carried value plus one; otherwise write the carried value unchanged. e.g. 1
inst.subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and the cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list, the robot is holding the cube: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open, all cubes on the table): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the current table position of that cube); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube.

Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up, at its current table position. At the first decision step the picked cube is identified in the DEMONSTRATION STEPS by the gripper's own [y, x] at the frame where it is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%: the cube listed nearest that spot (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames and the cube that reappears beside the gripper at put-down confirm it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). That cube's identity is then followed frame by frame through the rest of the demonstration, including every shuffle frame, by nearest-position matching between consecutive frames: when two cubes move at once they are exchanging places and each keeps its own identity along its own arc, so the picked cube ends where its arc ends, not where it started (two consecutive swaps of the same pair return it to its original spot). The value is its position in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step: if the execution steps since the previous decision step show a cube 'held in the gripper' and then released (fingers reopen to 100% near height 0.02), the value is that cube's table position in the scene at this decision step; otherwise it is the position of the listed cube nearest the previous value (within about 10 px), or the previous value unchanged if none is listed. 'Lifted off the table' lines are ignored. e.g. [85, 109]

At the first decision step the picked cube is identified in the DEMONSTRATION STEPS by the gripper's own [y, x] at the frame where it is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%: the cube listed nearest that spot (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames and the cube that reappears beside the gripper at put-down confirm it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). The 'picked' label is then carried through the shuffle one swap at a time, the shuffle being read as a sequence of STILL CONFIGURATIONS. A still configuration is a demonstration frame whose cube list is the same (within a few px) as the frame before it, with every cube on a resting spot and the gripper parked raised. Each still configuration is compared with the NEXT still configuration, pair by pair, up to and including the pair that ends at the last demonstration frame. Two consecutive still configurations that are identical are 'no swap'. Two that differ are exactly one swap: the two spots whose occupants changed have EXCHANGED occupants (the frames between them with cubes off every resting spot are mid-crossing frames). If the labelled cube was one of the two movers, it now rests on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never on its own; if it was not a mover, it stays where it is. Mid-crossing frames only show that a swap is happening and are never used to decide where the label lands; arc continuity may confirm which mover is which but never sends a mover back to its own spot. This is applied swap by swap to the last demonstration frame however many swaps occur and whoever the partners are (commonly three, sometimes one or two): two consecutive swaps of the same pair return the labelled cube to its original spot, and a later swap, possibly with a cube the gripper never touched, may move it away again; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. The label is never settled before the last demonstration frame, even when it is back on the pick spot. The cube resting on the original pick position after the shuffle is never chosen by that fact alone: once any swap touched that spot, the cube there is a different cube swapped in. The value is the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step the robot puts the cube back where it picked it, so the value is the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the previous value; if no such cube is listed (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or shown only as a 'lifted off the table' line while it settles), the value is the previous value unchanged. The gripper's position at the reopen frame, 'held in the gripper' coordinates and 'lifted off the table' coordinates are never used to locate it, and the value never moves to a resting cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]
picks_done

Count of completed grasps in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at a decision step whose execution steps show the gripper descend to about height 0.02 over the target cube with fingers closing from 100% to about 46% (or any frame saying a cube 'is held in the gripper'), and whose scene at the decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers still about 46% open. The table list at that scene is irrelevant: the held cube may still be listed at its old table position. It never changes at a decision step whose scene shows fingers 100% open, even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table' there. e.g. 2
target_colour

The colour word of the cube the demonstration picked up: 'red', 'blue', 'green', or 'cube' when the scene lists cubes without colour. It is fixed at the first decision step as the colour of the listed cube identified as the picked cube in the demonstration (the cube nearest the gripper at the lowest frame where the fingers first read about 46%), and it never changes at any later step. e.g. blue
target_cube

Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked, at its current table position. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%; the picked cube is the cube listed nearest the gripper's own [y, x] there (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames confirms it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). Then track the picked cube through the shuffle as a written ledger; do not read it off the final list. Step 1: write the pick spot P (the listed cube nearest the gripper at that lowest frame) and the spot where the cube is put back down (the listed cube reappearing beside the gripper when the fingers reopen); call that spot L. Step 2: from that frame onward, write out every STILL FRAME: a frame whose cube list is the same (within a few px) as the frame before it, with every cube on a resting spot, while the gripper is parked raised. Mid-crossing frames (cubes listed off every resting spot) are skipped and never used to decide where L lands. Step 2b: compare each still configuration to the NEXT still configuration, one pair at a time, writing one line for every pair until the pair that ends at the last demonstration frame. Where the two configurations are identical write 'no swap'. Where they differ, exactly two spots changed occupants: write 'swap k: spot X <-> spot Y; L now = ...' (if L is within about 10 px of X write Y, if of Y write X, otherwise unchanged). After the line for the last demonstration frame write 'swaps found: n' and only then stop. Expect commonly three swaps and sometimes one or two; never stop when L happens to be back on P, because a later swap can move it again, including a swap with a cube the gripper never touched. Two consecutive swaps of the same pair return L to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. Step 3: after the last frame, write the listed position in the scene at the start of execution nearest L (within about 10 px). Never write the cube resting on P when P appeared in any swap line: once any swap touched that spot, the cube resting there is a different cube. At every later decision step: the robot always puts the cube back where it picked it, so write the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the carried value. If there is none (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or listed only as 'lifted off the table' while it settles), copy the carried value unchanged. Do not locate it from the gripper position at the reopen frame, nor from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Never relocate to a cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby. e.g. [85, 109]
picks_done

Count of completed grasps. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, write the carried value plus one if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at about height 0.02 and fingers going from 100% to about 46% (or any 'is held in the gripper' line) AND the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers about 46% open (not 100%). Do not require the cube to be missing from the table list; it is usually still listed at its old position. Otherwise, and always when the fingers at the scene are 100% open (even if a cube is listed 'lifted off the table'), copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. 2
target_colour

At the first decision step (memory empty) write the colour word of the cube identified as the picked cube in the demonstration (the listed cube nearest the gripper at the lowest frame where the fingers first read about 46%): 'red', 'blue', 'green', or 'cube' when the list has no colours. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. blue
inst.subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for N times' (two, three, ...) means N pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step and tracked through the shuffle swaps). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%), the robot is holding the cube, regardless of the table list (the held cube is usually still listed at its old position): choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open; the robot holds nothing even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table', which is a cube just released and settling): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube as updated at this step (after a put-down this is the current position of the cube the execution steps showed released); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Always point at target_cube as updated at this step. When target_cube is absent from the resting list at this step (held or still settling), still point at target_cube itself, never at any other listed cube.

VideoPlaceButton.label: Initial
fields: target_before_button

The [y, x] of the target that the demonstration placed the cube on immediately before the button was pressed. Found by reading the whole demonstration: locate the first demonstration frame where the fingers go to 0% open (the gripper then descends onto the button and the button's y shifts, that is the press); take the last cube release before that frame (fingers widen from ~46% to ~100% while the gripper is low, height under 0.05); the cube's position at that release is the placement point; the field holds the coordinates of the target entry nearest that placement point as listed in the scene at the start of execution. Written at the first decision step and never changed afterwards. e.g. [126, 145]
cube_placed

Whether the robot itself has already dropped the goal cube onto target_before_button during execution. 'no' at every step until the decision step whose execution steps show the robot release the cube (fingers widen back to ~100% while low) with the cube lying within about 6 pixels of target_before_button; 'yes' from that step on. e.g. no
target_before_button

If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is unknown (first step, demonstration shown), compute it from the demonstration steps: find the first demonstration frame whose fingers read 0% open (the gripper is closing on nothing to press the button; the next frames show it low over the button); look backwards from there for the last frame where the fingers went from ~46% open to ~100% open with height under 0.05 (a release); the cube's position in that frame is the placement point; among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, pick the one nearest that placement point and write its [y, x]. e.g. [126, 145]
cube_placed

'no' at the first step and at every step until the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to ~100% while the gripper height is under 0.05 and the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of target_before_button; from that step on write 'yes'. e.g. no
inst.subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red or blue); call it the goal cube. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a marker telling you which target to use. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, target_before_button unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): first compute target_before_button from the demonstration as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to target_before_button (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [127, 146]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of target_before_button (it may be hidden), point at target_before_button itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and target_before_button is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on target_before_button: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.

PatternLock.label: Initial
fields: plan

The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces, written at the first decision step from the demonstration steps and copied unchanged at every later step. Derive it from the highlighted targets: the first highlighted target at demo t=0 is the start; each time a new target becomes highlighted during the demo, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (using the coordinates at the first frame each appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. e.g. ["E", "D", "G", "H"]
moves_done

How many of the planned moves the robot has finished executing by the scene at this step. 0 at the first decision step (nothing executed yet); at every later decision step it is the previous value plus one, since each decision step follows exactly one completed move. e.g. 2
plan

The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces. If this step shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS (the first step, memory empty), build it now and never change it afterwards: the highlighted target at demo t=0 is the start; each time a different target becomes highlighted in the demo frames, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (coordinates at the frame it first appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. If the step shows no demonstration, copy the carried-in plan exactly. e.g. ["E", "D", "G", "H"]
moves_done

How many planned moves have been finished by the scene at this step. Write 0 when the step shows demonstration steps and the carried memory is empty (first step). Otherwise the step shows execution steps of one completed move, so write the carried-in moves_done plus one. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal: Every episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory and the demonstration shown; the subgoal there is the first letter of the plan just built from the demonstration (plan index 0). At every decision step, the subgoal is the letter of plan at index moves_done (0-based, where moves_done is the value written at THIS step: 0 at the first step, carried value plus one at later steps). So the first step performs plan[0], the second step plan[1], and so on. No subgoal needs a point. After a move finishes, the next decision step always advances to the next plan letter regardless of where the gripper ended; never repeat or skip. If moves_done is at or beyond the length of the plan (nothing remains), repeat the last plan letter. If the plan could not be built (no demonstration visible and empty plan), derive the direction from the two highlighted targets currently visible if there are two (direction from the older-looking one near the gripper to the other, same dy/dx rule), otherwise choose A: move forward. In any other unforeseen situation, pick plan[moves_done] if it exists, else A.

BinFill.label: Initial
fields: deposited_count

The cumulative number of requested-color cubes released from the gripper into the bin during execution. Initially 0. Increment at the first act cycle whose incoming motion includes the completed release of a carried requested-color cube above the bin, not at the cycle that merely chooses the opening command. Count the release even when the cube disappears into the dark bin and its final resting position is invisible. A cycle containing both release and retreat counts once. Do not count grasps, transfers with the gripper closed, newly appearing tabletop cubes, or subsequent views of an already completed release. Retain the count through retreat and button pressing. e.g. 2
deposited_count

Initialize to 0 when memory is empty. Otherwise carry the incoming count forward. Add one when this cycle's motion frames show a requested-color cube carried over the bin being released as the fingers open, with the current hand empty. This includes a motion that also retreats after opening. The release must occur in the incoming motion: an already empty open hand above the bin is not another release. Do not increment for a command you are about to issue, a grasp, a closed-hand transfer, or new cubes appearing on the table. If no steps executed, retain the count unchanged. Keep the count after reaching the requested total and throughout button pressing. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal:
Read the requested color and quantity N from the goal each cycle. Use deposited_count plus any release visibly completed in the current incoming motion to determine how many deposits are now complete; do not count a release twice. Start with an open hand and zero deposits. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views, using the tabletop plane and cube geometry rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide. Locate the bin by its opening and the stop button by its gray circular top on a light square base. Re-estimate positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. Robot right is negative world y.

When fewer than N cubes have been deposited and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible requested-color tabletop cube. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above a cube; do not switch to another cube simply because new cubes appear. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and yaw aligned with a cube edge, choosing the equivalent square orientation within roughly [-0.7854,0.7854]. When already above that cube near z=0.15, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Use the wrist view to refine the same cube's center rather than descending at an inaccurate reported approach position.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the world xy center of the bin opening at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the current orientation. When the carried cube is above the bin at release height, command open at the centered release position. This is a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. If the target would be identical to the current TCP position, add a 0.003 m vertical displacement so opening executes.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When N deposits are complete and the release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, close the empty gripper at that approach position, adding a 0.003 m vertical displacement if needed to ensure a nonzero motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If no suitable cube is currently available before the quota is reached, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If an object needed for localization is occluded, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Never press the stop button before the requested number of deposits.

Do not increment when merely choosing the opening command, for grasps or closed transfers, or for later views of a completed release. Preserve otherwise, including through button pressing. e.g. 2

held_color

Color of the cube currently held: none, blue, green, or red. Initially none. Set to the cube's color at the first cycle showing a successful grasp. Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary occlusion while possession remains supported. Clear to none at the first cycle showing the hand empty after release or loss. Record observed possession, not a selected grasp target or an opening command about to execute. Deposit-count annotations retain their existing completed-release timing. e.g. red
bin_center

World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initially unknown. Set at the first cycle whose available calibrated views reliably constrain the center using geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks. Retain through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Revise only when reliable current geometry establishes a correction or an observed displacement of the bin. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. Use only geometry available by this cycle; do not backfill from later views or substitute recorded action destinations for visual reconstruction. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]
deposited_blue

Include only when blue is requested. Initialize to 0 when memory is empty; otherwise carry forward. Increment once when this cycle's incoming motion shows either a blue cube carried over the bin followed by an empty open hand, or a blue cube separating or falling directly below the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand. The sampled frames need not show the finger-opening transition itself. Require evidence of a new release from this hand over the bin; a stationary tabletop cube below the hand or an unrelated falling cube is not release evidence. Identify color from the carried or newly released cube, not remaining tabletop objects. Alternatively, when incoming held_color is blue, count a newly established transition to an empty open hand over the bin in the executed incoming release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere, even if all sampled frames omit the cube. Use incoming held_color before clearing it. This is an alternative evidence test for the same release, not an additional increment; an already empty hand or a no-step motion does not qualify. Count even if the resting cube is hidden and even if the motion includes retreat. Never increment for the command about to be issued, an already empty hand, a grasp, a closed transfer, retreat without a new release, or a motion executing no steps. Preserve through button pressing. e.g. 2

held_color

Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary visual occlusion while possession remains supported. bin_center

World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initialize to unknown. When this cycle's calibrated views reliably constrain the center using the action instruction's geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks, write that center immediately. Unknown is reserved for genuinely underconstrained geometry, not ordinary pixel-estimation uncertainty. When both views clearly show the opening, identify corresponding inner-rim corners in consistent cyclic order, triangulate them using the respective camera calibrations, and fit a horizontal rectangle. Check its reprojections against the visible inner rim and compute its world xy center from opposing corners. Never match an outer-rim corner to an inner-rim corner. Accept the fit when plausible corner fits constrain the center within 0.01 m in each world coordinate; exact pixel agreement is not required. This two-view test does not exclude the action instruction's geometrically constrained single-view reconstruction. Otherwise retain the incoming value through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Update an established value only when reliable current geometry supports a correction or establishes bin displacement. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. A cropped view or partial occlusion alone does not invalidate the retained center. Do not overwrite it with the centroid of a visible dark fragment, an occluding silhouette, measured TCP position, or the destination of an action being selected. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]
inst.subgoal:
Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's newly completed release in the current incoming motion, exactly once, using the memory instruction's sparse-frame evidence test. A carried cube followed by an empty open hand, or a cube visibly separating or falling from the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand, can establish the release without a sampled finger-opening transition. Also apply the memory instruction's incoming-held_color test when the released cube is absent from all incoming samples. Evaluate that test before clearing held_color, and compute completion from the resulting per-color counts, not from outgoing held_color. Multiple evidence tests for one release still produce only one increment. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: identify their four top-face corners, intersect the calibrated corner rays with the plane at approximately z=0.04, and fit a square in world coordinates. Use the fitted square's center for approach xy and the z=0.02 grasp, and its world-space edges for feasible edge-aligned yaw. When both views show the face, check the same fitted square against both views. Apply this procedure also to small faces in a high wrist view. Use the top face, not the whole colored patch or visible silhouette; reject fits biased toward a visible side face. Preserve the existing approached-cube identity and orientation through descent and lift. For the bin center, use a reliable current reconstruction when available; otherwise use incoming bin_center unless current observations establish that the bin moved. Partial occlusion or cropping alone does not invalidate a retained center. To obtain or reliably correct the center, reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening using the available calibrated current views. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Prefer reliable two-view correspondences between actual inner-rim corners or edge intersections: triangulate them and fit their common horizontal plane. For a clearly visible opening, match inner-rim corners in consistent cyclic order and apply the bin_center memory instruction's horizontal-rectangle fit and reprojection acceptance test. Do not match inner-rim corners to outer-rim corners. Ordinary pixel-estimation uncertainty does not justify unknown or a visibility-recovery motion when plausible fits already constrain the center within 0.01 m in each world coordinate; exact pixel agreement is not required. When such correspondences are unavailable, accept a single-view reconstruction if visible geometry constrains it. Identify actual table-contact base corners and their corresponding vertical wall edges; intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit corresponding upper corners along the world-vertical lines through those base corners to determine the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges and reconstruct obscured portions only where the fitted geometry constrains them. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and verify reprojection against all available visible rim segments, including partial wrist edges. Do not shift the center toward a visible side wall, use the centroid of an exposed dark fragment, average image centroids across cameras, treat occluding silhouettes as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. A cropped wrist view or partial opening occlusion alone does not require visibility recovery. Use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below only when neither current geometry nor a valid retained bin_center supplies a reliable center; do not invent a numeric rim height. Use the center selected by this current-reconstruction-or-memory rule consistently for closed transfer and separate release at z=0.20 and for retreat at [bin_x-0.10,bin_y,0.20]. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base. Fit the circular top in its world plane at approximately z=0.02 using calibrated rays from its visible boundary, and verify the fitted circle's reprojection against the other current view when available. Use the fitted world xy center for approach, empty-gripper closing, and press; do not use the square base or a rounded whole-object centroid. Re-estimate cube and button positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. For the bin, apply the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule rather than requiring fresh localization. Robot right is negative world y.

When any color quota remains outstanding and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible tabletop cube of an eligible color. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above an eligible cube; do not switch cubes or colors simply because new cubes appear. Never select another cube of a color whose quota is already satisfied. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and a feasible yaw aligned with a cube edge. Do not constrain yaw to [-0.7854,0.7854]. Re-estimate edge alignment for each newly selected cube rather than carrying over the previous cube's yaw, and preserve the selected orientation through descent and lift. When already above an eligible cube near z=0.15, identify the approached cube by projecting [current_tcp_x,current_tcp_y,0.04] into the current wrist image with its calibration. Identify the eligible top face nearest that projection, cross-checking world-space proximity and the incoming approach frames. Neither the wrist image center nor the largest visible cube is the alignment reference. Refine that same cube's top-face center at approximately z=0.04, then descend at its world xy to z=0.02 and close, preserving the approached cube's edge-aligned orientation. Do not switch to another prominent cube or descend at an inaccurate measured approach xy.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the world xy center of the bin opening supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the measured grasp orientation. After the closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20 above the bin, use that same rule to obtain the opening center and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting any residual lateral error in that waypoint. The target is the opening center, not the measured TCP xy. Opening remains a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. Correct both lateral coordinates before testing whether the centered target would produce no motion; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only in that case.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, including a release established using incoming held_color without a sampled separation, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Compute this offset from the bin center supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule, never from measured TCP xy. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, re-localize the gray circular button-top center using the calibrated circle fit in the approximately z=0.02 plane and its available second-view reprojection check. Use the circular top, not the surrounding square base. Command [button_x,button_y,0.15,-3.1416,0,0] and close the empty gripper. Correct the target before testing the nonzero-motion requirement; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only if the corrected target would otherwise produce no motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If any color quota remains outstanding but no suitable cube of an eligible color is currently available, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If occlusion leaves an object needed for localization genuinely underconstrained after using the available calibrated views and visible geometry, and for the bin no valid retained bin_center supplies its center, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Do not make this recovery motion merely because the wrist view crops the object or part of it is hidden. Never press the stop button before every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is complete.

PickXtimes.label: Initial
fields: placements_completed

Number of completed placements of the instructed cube on the target. Initialize to 0. Increment once at the first cycle showing the gripper opened after lowering the held cube onto the target, not at the cycle commanding that lowering. Keep the count through withdrawal and subsequent regrasping. A cube merely remaining on the target does not increment it. The initial placement counts toward the instructed total. e.g. 2
milestone

Most recently observed manipulation milestone, using exactly these values: start, cube_hover, cube_grasped, cube_lifted, target_hover, cube_released, release_retracted, button_hover, button_closed, button_pressed, button_retracted. Initialize to start. Update on the cycle showing completion of the corresponding motion or gripper change, never when its command is issued. cube_hover means the open hand has completed its dedicated alignment above the cube; cube_grasped means fingers have closed around it at pickup height; cube_lifted means it has been raised to transport height; target_hover means the subsequent target alignment has completed; cube_released means the hand has opened at placement height; release_retracted means the open hand has withdrawn to transport height. The button values respectively mean arrival above the button, empty gripper closure there, downward contact, and withdrawal. Retain the value if no motion or relevant change occurred. e.g. "cube_lifted"
placements_completed

Initialize to 0 with empty memory. Increment once when this cycle shows the previously held instructed cube lowered onto the target and the fingers now opened, with incoming milestone cube_lifted or target_hover. This is the observed release, not the command to release. Do not increment on withdrawal, on seeing the cube still on the target, or on a zero-step action. Otherwise carry the count unchanged. The initial placement counts toward the instructed total. e.g. 2
milestone

Initialize to start. Record only achieved events visible in this cycle's motion frames and current state. From start or release_retracted, completion of open-hand alignment above the instructed cube gives cube_hover. Closure around that cube at low height gives cube_grasped; raising it to about 0.15 m gives cube_lifted. A subsequent high target-alignment motion gives target_hover. From cube_lifted or target_hover, lowering and opening over the target gives cube_released; the subsequent open-hand ascent gives release_retracted. Once the placement count has reached the requested total, arrival above the button gives button_hover; closure of the empty fingers there gives button_closed; descent into button contact gives button_pressed; ascent after contact gives button_retracted. Use incoming milestone to distinguish a pickup alignment from withdrawal and a target alignment from the initial lift, even when their endpoints are nearly identical. Retain the incoming value if no relevant event occurred, including explicitly zero-step actions. e.g. "cube_lifted"
inst.subgoal:
Read the instructed color and total N from the goal. N is the total number of placements, including the first, not N additional repetitions. Use the observed milestone and updated placement count for the following rules. Estimate world positions from calibrated front and wrist images: identify the instructed cube, purple target-ring center, and gray button on its white base. Use table-plane projection for the target and account for cube height when locating its center. Refine with the wrist view; do not confuse its image center with the TCP projection. Never substitute another colored cube. Orient the hand downward, roll approximately -3.1416 and pitch 0, with yaw aligned to the cube's horizontal edges for grasping. Preserve that orientation during carrying and release.

At start, move with open fingers above the instructed cube's current center at z=0.15 m. At release_retracted with placements_completed < N, similarly make a dedicated open-hand alignment at z=0.15 m above that same cube, now on the target; do not return to its original location. At cube_hover, descend to the cube center's x,y at z=0.02 m and close. At cube_grasped, raise the cube vertically to z=0.15 m with fingers closed, using the observed cube/grasp center for x,y.

At cube_lifted, move closed to the target center at z=0.15 m before lowering. This alignment is needed even for repeated placements with only a few millimeters of displacement. If the target-hover waypoint differs from the current TCP position by less than 2 mm, omit that redundant motion and lower directly. At target_hover, lower at the target center to commanded z=0.005 m and open. Contact may leave the actual TCP higher than the commanded height; do not repeatedly force it down. At cube_released, withdraw vertically above the target to z=0.15 m, keeping fingers open. Always withdraw after the final placement as well.

At release_retracted with placements_completed >= N, move above the button center at z=0.15 m with open fingers and orientation [-3.1416,0,0]. At button_hover, close the empty gripper while maintaining alignment and approximately this height. At button_closed, descend at the button center to commanded z=0.0075 m with fingers closed. At button_pressed, retract to z=0.15 m with fingers closed. Contact commonly stops the TCP near z=0.025 m; treat observed button contact as the press rather than demanding the commanded depth be reached.

Every waypoint must differ from the current TCP position by at least 2 mm. For a gripper-only change or otherwise necessary near-identical hover alignment, add a small upward displacement, about 3–5 mm, while keeping the intended x,y. Do not advance memory because a waypoint was merely requested. Allow ordinary tracking error when recognizing completed motions.

If an unexpected state occurs, use visible evidence rather than inventing progress: if a grasp failed, reopen and realign above the instructed cube; if holding it below transport height, lift before lateral travel; if placement or button contact is occluded, withdraw safely to reveal the result without incrementing the count speculatively. Re-estimate positions from the newly exposed scene and resume the applicable rule. After button_retracted, do not restart cube manipulation; if execution continues and the button was not visibly activated, realign above it and retry the press. Do not wait without a specific observation or physical event to resolve.

Allow ordinary small tracking errors and very short nonzero alignment motions when recognizing completion, but do not use that broader completion tolerance to decide whether alignment can be omitted. Never recognize target_hover merely because alignment was commanded, or because direct descent was selected. Following direct descent, retain cube_lifted until release is observed, then apply the existing release milestone and placement-count rules. At target_hover, re-estimate the target-ring center and lower at that center to commanded z=0.005 m and open, correcting lateral tracking error during descent rather than copying achieved hover TCP x,y. Contact may leave the actual TCP higher than the commanded height; do not repeatedly force it down. At cube_released, withdraw vertically above the target to z=0.15 m, keeping fingers open. Always withdraw after the final placement as well.

At release_retracted with placements_completed >= N, move above the reliably localized current button center, or button_center_xy when the current view is unreliable, at z=0.15 m with open fingers and orientation [-3.1416,0,0]. At button_hover, close the empty gripper at that independently localized button center x,y and nominal z=0.15 m, correcting any hover tracking offset. At button_closed, descend at the independently localized button center to commanded z=0.0075 m with fingers closed; do not substitute achieved hover TCP x,y. At button_pressed, retract at the button center x,y to z=0.15 m with fingers closed. Contact commonly stops the TCP near z=0.025 m; treat observed button contact as the press rather than demanding the commanded depth be reached.

Construct the center-corrected waypoint first, then apply the 2 mm minimum positional-displacement safeguard. If its lateral or vertical correction already supplies at least 2 mm of displacement from the current TCP, do not add an upward offset. For a gripper-only change or otherwise necessary near-identical hover alignment below that threshold, add a small upward displacement, about 3–5 mm, while keeping the intended center x,y.  Do not advance memory because a waypoint was merely requested. Allow ordinary tracking error when recognizing completed motions.

If an unexpected state occurs, use visible evidence rather than inventing progress: if a grasp failed, reopen and realign above the instructed cube; if holding it below transport height, lift before lateral travel; if placement or button contact is occluded, withdraw safely to reveal the result without incrementing the count speculatively. Re-estimate positions from the newly exposed scene and resume the applicable rule. After button_retracted, do not restart cube manipulation; if execution continues and the button was not visibly activated, realign above it and retry the press. Do not wait without a specific observation or physical event to resolve.

SwingXtimes.label: Initial
fields: target_visits

Number of completed, ordered target visits while holding the instructed cube. Start at 0. Count arrivals in the order right, left, right, left, up to twice the requested repetition count. A visit is completed when the carried cube arrives above the corresponding target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m and that target activates red. Record the increment at the cycle showing that arrival, not at the cycle commanding it. Do not count repeated frames of an activation, pickup, release, or button operations. Retain the final count thereafter. Thus all episodes have 0 at cycles 1–4; subsequent arrival cycles have 1, 2, 3, 4, and, for three repetitions, 5, 6. e.g. 2
target_visits

Initialize to 0 when memory is empty. Let N be the repetition count in the instruction. If the carried-in count is below 2N, the next uncounted target is right for an even count and left for an odd count. Increment once when this cycle shows the instructed cube held above that target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m, with the target activated red. Use the current endpoint and motion frames to confirm arrival; an activation on the other side is not a new visit. Otherwise retain the count, including during release and button operations. Never increment merely because a waypoint is being issued, and never increment on a zero-step unchanged cycle. e.g. 2
inst.subgoal:
Start with empty memory, an open hand, and target_visits initialized to zero. Read the cube color and repetition count N from the instruction. Update target_visits from observed arrivals before selecting the action; do not anticipate completion of the action you are about to issue. Right means smaller world y, appearing on the left of the front image; left means larger world y. Locate the two circular targets, the instructed cube, and the gray button on its square base using the calibrated images. Convert image locations to world coordinates using their appropriate surface heights, rather than treating image displacement as world displacement. Use the wrist view for fine localization. Target centers lie essentially on the tabletop; account for the cube's height when estimating its center and for the button's raised surface when localizing it. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.

When target_visits is zero and the instructed cube is not held, approach vertically above its center at z=0.15 m, gripper open, with roll approximately pi, pitch zero and yaw aligned to its square edges. If already above it at that height, descend to its center at z=0.02 m and close. A grasp is evidenced by the cube between the fingers and finger positions approximately 0.018–0.019 m, rather than an empty fully closed hand. When the newly grasped cube is still low, lift vertically to z=0.15 m, maintaining the grasp and cube-aligned orientation.

When holding the cube clear of the table and target_visits is less than 2N, command the center of the next required target at z=0.10 m: right if target_visits is even, left if odd. Keep the gripper closed and preserve the current orientation. Move directly between target centers at this height; do not lower onto the table, release, return to the pickup position, or insert a lift between visits. A confirmed red activation counts as arrival despite ordinary TCP tracking error; do not demand exact coincidence with the commanded coordinates. If the required target has not activated and arrival is uncertain, refine its center from visible geometry and complete that same visit rather than skipping it.

When target_visits equals 2N and the cube is still held at the final left target, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.07 m and open. When the cube has been released and the open hand remains low there, retreat vertically to approximately z=0.15 m while staying open. When the released cube is on the final target and the hand is clear, move above the button center at z=0.15 m, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper at the button's nominal approach position. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion; if that nominal position is too close to the reported TCP, add a 5 mm upward displacement. When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the button center to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation. Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract above the same button to z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward.

For an ambiguous or otherwise unmatched situation, use current images and gripper state to recover the applicable geometric condition: refine alignment, or raise vertically to safe clearance if low and obstructed. Preserve a held cube and the visit count. Do not invent completed visits or restart the alternating sequence. Never issue an identical-pose action, and do not wait without an observable task-related purpose.

When target_visits is zero and the instructed cube is not held, localize its top square face for both the initial hover and grasp descent, excluding visible side faces. Where the four top-face corners can be identified, project each corner this way and average the resulting world points to obtain the face center; otherwise project the identified top-face center. StopCube.label: Initial
fields: motion_reference

An ordered list of execution keyframes documenting the initial cube motion. At the first cycle write [E0]. At the first cycle showing actual elapsed motion, append that cycle's displayed front-camera frame labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Freeze this list thereafter. These frames preserve the initial endpoint, early motion and its absolute timing, allowing the oscillation period and numbered future target passages to be inferred even when later images show the same positions again. They also retain the unobstructed button location. Do not select frames from future cycles. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]
motion_reference

With empty memory write [E0]. If the incoming list contains only E0 and this cycle shows that execution time has advanced, append all displayed execution front-camera labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged. A zero-step action does not trigger appending. Once the initial motion frames have been appended, never append further frames or replace the list. Use the stored images and their absolute step labels as the reference for reconstructing the cube's periodic motion. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]
inst.subgoal:
Start by locating the gray circular button on its white base, the colored moving cube, and the purple target. Infer the button's world xy from the calibrated images and its tabletop base, using the wrist view to refine localization. Do not use image left/right as robot left/right. When the TCP is initially high and has not approached the button, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. Use the button center, not the slightly displaced achieved hover TCP, for subsequent commanded xy.

While hovering approximately 0.15 m above the button, keep the gripper closed and determine when to press. Read the requested ordinal N from the goal. Use motion_reference together with the current motion frames and absolute elapsed_control_steps to reconstruct the cube's oscillation. The cube starts at one endpoint and moves smoothly back and forth; count a passage through the target in either direction, not a complete round trip. Fit the motion in world tabletop coordinates rather than assuming constant image velocity. In these trajectories the target is the midpoint of the oscillation: for full period P, passage times are P/4 + (N-1)P/2. Infer P from observed motion, not from the requested ordinal or the cube's color. The demonstrated periods include 120, 160 and 240 control steps. Initial and current frames should agree with the inferred phase; do not reset the passage count when the cube returns to an earlier-looking position.

Begin the downward press about 20 control steps before the requested target passage. Thus compute the press-start step S = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 - L. Use L = 20 steps normally; use approximately 22 steps for a button toward the robot's far right, near y = -0.19 m, where the demonstrated descent needs slightly more lead. This gives press starts of 400 for the fourth passage with P=240, 280 for the third with P=240, 190 for the fourth with P=120, approximately 178 for the third with P=160 at the far-right button, and 340 for the fifth with P=160. These are consequences of measured periods and button geometry, not episode identifiers.

If the current step t is below S, wait min(30, round(S-t)) control steps in place, maintaining the closed gripper. Do not take an extra full 30-step wait when fewer steps remain. If t has reached S and the hand is still hovering, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. The press waypoint is intentionally below the contact-limited achieved TCP height; do not substitute the observed contact height for the command. Account for motion time: waiting until the cube visibly reaches the target before starting the descent is too late.

If the TCP is down at the button, approximately z=0.025 m, following a visible descent and contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0], keeping the gripper closed. Do not press again simply because the cube remains near the target. A stopped cube after contact calls for retraction or, if already retracted, a short wait for termination.

If observations do not support a reliable period, compare retained initial motion with the current frames and wait a short interval, at most 10 steps, to disambiguate direction and speed rather than pressing on an uncertain passage. If the button is temporarily occluded, recover its position from the retained unobstructed frames. If alignment is genuinely lost, move to the safe button-centered hover before attempting contact. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when no movement is needed.

Estimate container center and orientation using calibrated image geometry, preferably its top-face corners and the wrist view. Account for the height of the top face rather than projecting its center onto the tabletop. Apply these state-dependent rules, using completed_lifts updated from the motion just observed:

If the hand is closed around a container at low grasp height, lift that container to z=0.20 with the gripper closed. Center the lift over the container's current x,y, preserving its aligned yaw. This rule takes precedence over selecting another target.

If a completed requested lift leaves a container held at z approximately 0.20 and further requested colors remain, lower it vertically at the current TCP x,y to z=0.070 and open the gripper at arrival; preserve the current orientation. Do not carry it to the next target or drop it from approach height.

If the gripper is open near z=0.070 following that replacement, retreat vertically at the current x,y to z=0.146 with the gripper open and orientation preserved. The next target is not approached laterally until this clearance is reached.

Otherwise, with an empty open hand, select requested color number completed_lifts+1. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20, move to its center x,y at z=0.20 with aligned downward orientation and the gripper open. This includes the initial high pose and the post-release clearance pose. If already above the selected container at approach height, descend to its center x,y at z=0.0633 and close at arrival. Use calibrated camera geometry, not image-side labels, to estimate world coordinates. The front image's right is world +y. Recover object centers using their physical heights rather than projecting elevated top faces onto the table. The retained uncovered_scene supplies the cube-to-container association after the cubes disappear; compare its cube locations with the current containers, allowing for their top-face height and perspective. Extra containers are distractors. Do not infer that container appearance means the button has been pressed.

Apply the following rules to the observed situation. Use current contact evidence together with incoming button_pressed to recognize that the press has occurred; the outgoing memory is not a prerequisite for recognizing current contact. Likewise, use incoming completed_pickups together with any qualifying lift completion observed this cycle to determine the number of completed pickups for action selection. A commanded lift is not a completed pickup. Read the requested color order from the goal; with an empty hand, select the next uncompleted color. Never repeat a completed pickup or the completed button press.

Button-hover arrival tolerance determines which operation is next, not the button's coordinates. For every button approach, closing, pressing, opening, and retraction command, reconstruct the circular button's actual world center from calibrated current imagery at its physical height. Never substitute the measured hover TCP x,y for that center. Closing at hover uses that center at z=0.15; pressing uses that center at z=0.0075. Preserve the nonidentical-waypoint safeguard for gripper-only changes.

Before pressing: if the hand is not at the button hover, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper open. Treat an approach ending within roughly 1.5 cm horizontally and 1 cm vertically as arrival. If at this hover with open fingers, command the same nominal hover with gripper closed. If at hover with closed fingers and button_pressed is false, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper closed. Do not repeatedly drive downward when the fingers have contacted the button: the realized TCP may stop near z=0.024 rather than the commanded height.

After observed button contact, or with button_pressed true: if still low over the button, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0], keeping the gripper closed. At the button hover with closed fingers, open the gripper at that nominal hover. At the button hover with open fingers, move directly to the target-container hover, not back down onto the button.

The target is the container covering the next uncompleted requested color in uncovered_scene. Associate the remembered cube locations with current containers using calibrated world coordinates, not raw image-centroid overlap. Identify the four corners of the same horizontal square top face, distinguishing them from lower side-wall corners, overhanging edges, and the whole container's outer silhouette. Reconstruct each selected top-face corner explicitly using its pixel p=[u,v,1], camera intrinsics K, and world-to-camera extrinsics [R|t]. Compute the world camera center C=-R^T t and world ray direction d=R^T K^-1 p, then intersect the ray with the horizontal top/grasp plane h approximately 0.0634 m: X=C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Use the fixed front-camera extrinsics for front pixels and the current wrist-camera extrinsics for current wrist pixels. Average the reconstructed coplanar corners to obtain target_x and target_y; the intersection of the reconstructed diagonals provides a consistency check. Reproject the reconstructed square into the available current calibrated views and verify that its corners and edges match the selected horizontal top face. Resolve inconsistent corner selections or arithmetic before issuing the waypoint. Use this reconstructed center for the z=0.20 hover and subsequent grasp. Do not approximate world x from image row, intersect elevated top-face rays with the table plane, average the whole image silhouette, or combine corners at different heights. Derive yaw from the reconstructed world-plane edges, not image-plane slopes. The remembered cube location determines container identity, not its elevated grasp center. Choose a downward orientation [3.1416, 0, yaw] aligned with opposing grasp faces. Among equivalent square-aligned yaws, choose the one requiring the smallest absolute wrapped rotation from the current measured TCP yaw. Preserve this alignment through descent and lift, refining it from visible world-plane edges without switching to another square-equivalent alignment. Apply the same current-yaw preference when transferring between requested containers after release clearance; do not reset the preference to zero. Refine the estimate with current wrist geometry, distinguishing the optical center from the TCP projection. Use this reconstructed container center for both the open-hand hover [target_x, target_y, 0.20, 3.1416, 0, yaw] and the descent to z approximately 0.0634 with closure on arrival. When already at the target hover with open fingers, descend rather than repeating the hover. Do not copy an offset realized hover position into the grasp command or substitute the remembered cube's image centroid for the elevated container's current top center. Apply the held-container return and release-clearance rules before any next-target approach or grasp.

When the fingers have closed around the target at grasp height, typically leaving about 0.018 m on each finger, lift to z=0.20 over the same grasp center with the same yaw and gripper closed. Do not treat selection of this waypoint as completion.

When the required container has actually reached approximately z=0.20 in a closed grasp and another requested pickup remains, return it over its original cube: command the current measured x,y at z=0.07, preserving the current orientation, and open on arrival. This return-and-release rule takes priority over approaching the next target. Preserve the completed pickup count even when the returned container conceals its cube.

With open fingers low over a returned, already completed container, retract vertically to approximately z=0.145 at the current x,y and orientation, keeping the gripper open. This release-clearance rule takes priority over grasp rules and the generic hover fallback. Once at this clearance height, move directly to the next uncompleted container's z=0.20 hover. Then descend, close, and lift according to the target rules. When the last requested pickup has actually been lifted, retain the closed grasp; do not return or release it. Never try to grasp a revealed cube.

For commands that only change the gripper, use the nominal hover target if it differs from the measured TCP by at least 2 mm. Otherwise add a 3 mm upward displacement so the waypoint is not identical to the current pose. Small execution errors do not imply a new task stage or require replaying an already completed press.

If alignment is uncertain, use the retained scene and current wrist/front geometry to refine the relevant object's location and make a corrective open-hand hover motion before descending. If a commanded motion explicitly executed no steps, preserve memory and retry the applicable rule with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. For an otherwise unmatched situation, safely raise the hand vertically to the relevant hover height, preserving a held object's closed grip, then reapply these observation-based rules. Do not wait without a specific observable purpose.

ButtonUnmask.label: Optimized
fields: uncovered_scene

Store the first execution frame showing the colored cubes before containers conceal them. Retain this same label throughout the episode. This preserves the association between the instructed cube color and the subsequently covering container, not a fixed container rank or image-side choice. In all supplied episodes this is E0. e.g. "E0"
button_pressed

Initially false. Change to true at the cycle showing completion of the closed-finger downward press on the button, and retain true thereafter. Contact ends with the TCP approximately 0.024 m above the table even though the commanded press height is 0.0075 m. Thus this field is false at cycles 1–3 and true at cycles 4–8 in every supplied episode. Record observed completion, not the selection of a future pressing waypoint. e.g. false
completed_pickups

The number of pickups completed in the goal's requested order. Initialize to 0. Increment once when the cycle shows the next required container actually lifted in a closed grasp to approximately z=0.20, exposing its cube. Do not increment on grasp closure or on selection of a lift waypoint. A continued hold or lowering of an already counted container does not count again. Retain the count through return, release, and retreat, even when the cube becomes concealed again. e.g. 1
uncovered_scene

With empty memory, store the label of the first current execution frame showing the exposed colored cubes. Thereafter copy the incoming label unchanged, including after containers appear. Use the retained image to identify where the cube named by the goal was concealed. e.g. "E0"
button_pressed

With empty memory initialize false. Set true when the current motion frames and robot state show the closed fingers have descended onto the circular button and reached contact, with TCP near z=0.024 m over its center. Otherwise copy the incoming value. Never set true merely because containers appeared, the fingers closed at hover height, or a downward press is being commanded. Once true, retain true. e.g. false
completed_pickups

With empty memory initialize to 0. Read the requested color order from the goal. Increment the incoming count once when this cycle's motion frames show the container for the next uncompleted requested color being lifted in a closed grasp to approximately z=0.20 and exposing its cube. Use the incoming count to identify which pickup qualifies. Do not count continued holding or lowering of an already completed pickup, grasp closure alone, or a lift that is only being commanded. Otherwise copy the incoming value, including through return, release, and retreat. e.g. 1
